#1794. Tottenham: Why Roberto De Zerbi must be tough on Luca Williams-Barnett despite dazzling debut

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

A weirdly comforting lull set in at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium as Spurs coasted home to victory over 10-man Crystal Palace.

Tottenham injury update: Bergvall, Mudryk, Savio latest return dates

Tottenham fans make Bentancur point as Arsenal star escapes red card

Sage makes sack admission as Crystal Palace future hangs in balance

Attention in some parts of the stadium had already turned to next week and a trip to Elland Road. But Roberto De Zerbi had one last trick up his sleeve to send Spurs supporters back home happy.

Young Luca Williams-Barnett, long touted as the next big prospect out of Spurs’ academy, was being readied for his Premier League debut.

In the same week Spurs’ greatest academy product lifted the Ballon d’Or, the time felt right for the 18-year-old to make his long-awaited top-flight bow.

De Zerbi has been patient with the teenage sensation, cautious not to throw him in while Spurs were struggling for results.

But as they edged closer to making it three wins in a row for the first time since February 2025, the Italian sensed an opportunity, introducing Williams-Barnett in the 88th minute to rapturous applause.

With the Palace backline tiring, having defended with a man less since the 13th minute, and spaces opening up, Williams-Barnett was in his element.

It was a highlight reel-worthy cameo from the 18-year-old, who should have grabbed an assist when he chopped inside Palace wing-back Anan Khalaili before charging to the byline and crossing for Mohammed Kudus.

Kudus got his finish all wrong, but the confidence and invention from Williams-Barnett was clear for all to see, and his performance had De Zerbi lauding him as a “very, very great talent” post-match.

The compliments did not stop there either, with Spurs goalkeeper Antonin Kinsky claiming “he has the quality, personality and all the potential to become a great player.”

Williams-Barnett is said to have impressed during first-team training. Unafraid to try things and showcase his undoubted talent, he has been taken under the wing of James Maddison.

De Zerbi believes Williams-Barnett has the right mix of confidence and arrogance to go to the very top, but the Spurs boss will also appreciate that the development of young players is not linear and he can not guarantee minutes.

For as much as Williams-Barnett dazzles with the ball at his feet, killing dead a long diagonal pass with his first touch against Palace, De Zerbi’s wingers need to show they are willing to work off the ball.

It was the right moment for him ... he has big quality, he’s very young but a great talent

This is a side of Williams-Barnett’s game he will need to develop, but there is no doubt he has the attitude and application to put himself in the frame for more regular minutes.

De Zerbi will be tough on him because he knows the talent he possesses, and this is what Williams-Barnett needs. From the jewel in the crown of the club’s academy, the boyhood Spurs fan must now mould into a selfless professional without losing that magic touch that gets fans off their seats.

That balance can be tricky. But with Spurs growing in confidence and moving up the Premier League table, there are likely to be more opportunities to impress.

It is important that Spurs manage Williams-Barnett correctly, and choosing whether to loan him out in January is the first of several key decisions they will need to take with his development.

Spurs have seen many players impress in the academy only to struggle to make the step up to senior football, and that is as much down to how they are managed as it is to their talent.

They can not afford to get it wrong with Williams-Barnett. His ability is comparable to some of the very best youngsters coming through the ranks in England right now.

#1792. Man United vs. Roma: How to watch, date, time, live stream and TV channel for Champions League clash

By Matt Law | 02 Nov 2026 13:13, Last updated: 02 Nov 2026 13:14

Manchester United will continue their Champions League league stage campaign with a clash against Roma on Tuesday night.

The 20-time English champions desperately need a positive result, but they will be welcoming a Roma side with four wins from their last five matches during a strong run of form.

Here, Sports Mole provides details of how to tune into the contest.

The Champions League match will kick off at 8pm UK time on Tuesday.

The Champions League match between Man United and Roma will be played at the English club's home stadium, Old Trafford.

The last clash between the two teams at Old Trafford came in the quarter-finals of the 2007-08 Champions League, with Man United recording a 1-0 victory to secure a 3-0 aggregate success and progress to the semi-finals.

The European game will not be broadcast live on TV in the UK.

The Champions League clash can be streamed live on Amazon's Prime Video.

Game-changing events will be posted on the PrimeVideoSport X account, while highlights will be uploaded to the Amazon Prime Video Sport YouTube channel later in the evening.

It has to turn for Man United at some point; the Red Devils are now nine games without a win in all competitions and have lost four of their last five during a horrendous run.

Michael Carrick has kept his job at the helm for now, but two more poor results against Roma and Aston Villa would surely see a change in the dug-out.

Man United are 20th in the overall Champions League table with three points from three matches, while Roma sit in 15th on four points.

Roma have won four of their last five matches during a strong run of form and will therefore enter this game full of confidence against a fragile Red Devils outfit.

Man United need a big performance and a big result - the fans deserve one - and it could be the perfect chance to bounce back under the lights at Old Trafford on Tuesday.

#1791. How Xabi Alonso conversation unleashed Chelsea's wildcard option

Your weekly briefing on Chelsea, featuring team news and expert analysis from Dom Smith

Late on at Stamford Bridge on Saturday and Estevao plays a give-and-go with Morgan Rogers, shooting powerfully towards the far corner but then jolting his head right up to the heavens in anguish as Manchester United’s Senne Lammens saves.

The Brazilian’s frustration in that moment is palpable, and quite understandable.

Already he had seen two goals disallowed for tight offsides, and he was having one of those days, he felt, when the ball just won’t go in for you. But failure to score on his much-belated first Premier League start of the season was not the key takeaway in the eyes of anyone but himself. He had made his impact.

Made his point, too. Estevao was one of the Premier League’s breakout stars last term but has had to wait so patiently for the chance to feel wanted and valued under Alonso.

Should that day have come earlier? Without question, it should. Geovany Quenda — also 19, but more raw than Estevao — struggled against Tottenham, and at Anfield in their Carabao Cup defeat last Wednesday, Chelsea were again crying out for Estevao’s devilment which was never summoned.

But Alonso had a plan; better late than never. He told him he would be starting against United almost a week in advance, ample time to prepare.

Estevao is the latest obsession back home in Brazil, already a gem for the national team under Carlo Ancelotti, and he had played as much this season for them as for his club until let loose on Michael Carrick’s unsturdy defence.

What of that creaking United backline there was left to unsettle, Estevao unsettled. The one constant when you hear people talking about the teen is mention of his uncanny ability to lift fans up off their seats. That was noticeable again as he drove into space, carrying the ball deep into United’s half, working the angle to shoot when he could but never happier than when hurtling into open turf with his impossibly low centre of gravity and the ball at his feet.

“Every time I got the ball I tried to give it to him, to show what he could do,” Cole Palmer said, still unrivalled as Chelsea’s main character but with an older-brotherly fondness for the wonderkid.

Fresh reports in Spain this week of interest from Barcelona in Estevao should come as no surprise, but Alonso insists his young star is going nowhere in January. As Chelsea prepare for Sunderland at the Stadium of Light, where they lost in Estevao’s absence on the final day of last season, it is now inconceivable that the youngster is left unused as often for the remainder of the season as he has been up to this point.

Alonso sees him as a right winger rather than a wing-back, and perhaps it is merely a reflection of his stiff competition with Palmer, Rogers and Joao Pedro — the front three that picks itself — that explains why a player with such prodigious talent has played so fleeting a part in Chelsea’s season. Whatever the reason, it has pained him.

The first of Estevao’s two disallowed goals was reminiscent of his stunner against Barca in the Champions League last term and his influence on Saturday was immense, surely enough to convince Alonso he can play the roles of impact sub or starting lineup wildcard as and when each best fits.

The Chelsea manager would do well to remember that keeping the Blues’ impressionable young star onside is important and keeping the club’s fanbase onside is critical all the same. The cheers were piercing when Estevao’s name was read out and whenever he ran at United. Patience shown, Estevao’s time has come.

#1788. Man United head coach Michael Carrick confirms Patrick Dorgu decision for Roma clash as 22-year-old makes timely return

By Matt Law | 02 Nov 2026 13:45, Last updated: 02 Nov 2026 13:47

Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick has said that Patrick Dorgu will not be involved in Tuesday's Champions League clash with Roma despite returning to training.

Dorgu has missed Man United's last six matches due to an injury that he sustained while representing Denmark during the September/October international break.

The 22-year-old was pictured back in training on Monday, though, fuelling rumours that a return to the squad against Roma was possible.

Carrick has confirmed that the Dane is not yet ready to return to action, but there is a chance that he could be involved against Aston Villa in the Premier League this weekend.

"Yeah, it was his first day with the group, great to have him back, but he won't be involved tomorrow. We'll see how he progresses for the week (for Villa)," Carrick told reporters.

Dorgu's return is timely given Man United's issues at left-back, with Luke Shaw still unavailable for selection.

Man United will also again be missing Benjamin Sesko and Marcus Rashford against Roma, while Manuel Ugarte is a long-term absentee for the 20-time English champions.

Lisandro Martinez is available, as his upcoming ban only relates to domestic matches, but it remains to be seen whether the Argentina international starts following his red card in the team's 2-0 defeat to Chelsea on Saturday afternoon.

When asked about possible concerns surrounding Martinez's commitment, Carrick said: "I've got no concerns about commitment at all. Things happen in football, sometimes you make mistakes, sometimes it goes well for you, but commitment is not an issue, for sure."

Carrick remains under major pressure due to the team's struggles this season. Indeed, the Red Devils are without a victory in their last nine games in all competitions.

"I know the players, I know what we’re capable of as a team… we’ve showed it in spells, showed it in bursts," Carrick added during his pre-Roma press conference.

Defeats to Roma and Aston Villa in the team's next two matches would likely spell the end of Carrick's time at the helm, but there is still an opportunity for the club's former midfielder to turn the campaign around.

#1787. 'Lucky': Arsenal get double referee verdict over Noni Madueke and Jurrien Timber incidents

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Arsenal have been told that Jurrien Timber was “lucky” to not concede a penalty in Sunday’s win over Liverpool, while Alexis Mac Allister has been labelled “embarrassing” for his clash with Noni Madueke.

The Dutchman pulled the shirt of Alexander Isak as the Liverpool striker attempted to get on the end of a cross, though Isak did not go to ground despite that contact preventing him getting to the ball.

Referee Andy Madley waved away Liverpool’s appeals and VAR did not intervene to overrule that decision.

Andoni Iraola was left bemused by the incident and revealed he will now have a very clear message for his players in the opposition’s box.

He said: "The answer is you have to dive, if you don't dive they won't call it."

Looking back on the pull from Timber, former referee Dermot Gallagher suggested that the error was from the officials on the pitch rather than VAR, as he indicated a penalty should have been awarded.

"It depends which angle you watch it from,” Gallagher told Sky Sports.

“The first angle, you see nothing. That is the referee's angle. The second angle, which is what VAR looks at, and it is a lot more damning.

"VAR looks at it in slow motion, which is another thing against him. In normal speed, he grabs and grabs him quickly but let's go. Does he do enough [for a penalty]?

"What is Timber's intention? He is on the wrong side of him. Does he do enough to stop him? He [Isak] will say yes, as he is close to the ball.

"VAR would be accused of re-refereeing if it is a penalty. It is a case of damned if they do and damned if they don't.

"It has to be the case of on-field. The more I watch it, the more I think he [Timber] has taken a big chance and has got lucky."

#1785. Big game players, big game performances: Player ratings for Milan-Inter from Italian papers

Last night’s win against Inter was proof of the quality within the AC Milan squad, so now it’s a case of continuing on the path upwards.

For Milan, a win in the derby wasn’t essential. Yes, it would always be a big help, but avoiding defeat was the priority, given a 10-point gap would’ve opened to the title leaders. Yet, the Rossoneri were brave and fought for three points, even if most would’ve taken one.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

A defining performance of the Ruben Amorim era so far, everyone played their role stupendously – and that includes the Portuguese, who tactically outclassed his counterpart. As a result, the scores from us were rather high in our post-match ratings.

Looking at the ratings from elsewhere, Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below) gave the performance an eight, also giving Amorim that score, too.

In terms of the players’ performances, Goncalo Ramos was the lowest, with a still passable score of a 6. However, Ardon Jashari and Davide Bartesaghi were also given these scores, understandable after coming off the bench.

With 6.5s, Koni De Winter, Yunus Musah and Alphadjo Cisse were all very solid, with the latter almost grabbing a fourth in the game. Mario Gila, Strahinja Pavlovic and Sankhoun Diawara were given 7s, as did Luka Modric and the first goalscorer Christian Pulisic.

The Diavolo’s French duo – Mike Maignan and Adrien Rabiot – were awarded a score of 7.5, whilst Diego Moreira was given an eight for his goal and two assists.

Moving to Corriere dello Sport, Amorim was given an eight again. Ramos scored the lowest again, at a six, whilst Musah, Diawara, Pavlovic and De Winter were given 6.5. Gila, Modric, Pulisic and Rabiot were given 7s. Then, Maignan was given a 7.5, Moreira, again, was given an 8/10.

Finally, Tuttosport’s ratings were largely the same. Ramos was given a downgrade to a 5/10, whilst Moreira was given another eight. The French goalkeeper kept his second-best position with a 7.5 – alongside Rabiot – thanks to his big saves, whilst Diawara was also given a bump up to a 7, thanks to an impressive derby debut.

Elsewhere, Gila, De Winter, Pavlovic, Musah and Pulisic were given 6.5s, Modric played a 7/10 game and Amorim was given a 7.5.

#1784. Manchester United have new injury concern as star spotted strapped up in training

Manchester United could be sweating over the fitness of Leny Yoro ahead of their Champions League clash with Roma.

The Red Devils welcome the Serie A side to Old Trafford on Tuesday as Michael Carrick looks to put a stop to his side’s nine-match winless run.

The under-fire head coach has seen pressure mount on his shoulders, and particularly after three straight defeats.

United were thrashed 4-1 and 3-0 by Como and Bournemouth respectively a fortnight ago, and a 2-0 loss at Chelsea followed last weekend, as Lisandro Martinez was sent off at Stamford Bridge and Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer got the goals to hand Xabi Alonso’s hosts all three points.

Now, attentions turn back to the continent, where United sit 20th after three games.

They have won once and lost their last two, against Atletico Madrid and Como, and they were handed a boost on Monday as Patrick Dorgu returned to team training ahead of the Roma encounter.

The Dane had been sidelined with a hamstring problem that he picked up on international duty in September, but his comeback will be hugely welcomed amid United’s lack of senior left-back options.

However, there was cause for concern as eagle-eyed fans spotted defender Yoro strapped up ahead of Tuesday’s game.

The Frenchman, who has filled in at right-back to accommodate for Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui’s shift to left-back, was once again fielded at full-back in west London over the weekend, where he played the full 90 minutes.

He was seen with strapping on his knee while training, but did not look in discomfort as he participated in various drills.

The Frenchman could well be reinstated at centre-back should Carrick look to rotate his defensive unit, with Martinez suspended for the upcoming Premier League clash against Aston Villa.

#1783. Arsenal: Ryan Gravenberch angers Liverpool fans with Jurrien Timber interaction

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Liverpool midfielder Ryan Gravenberch has faced criticism from supporters after appearing to like an Instagram post celebrating Arsenal’s victory at Anfield.

The Gunners secured a 1-0 win on Sunday, with Kai Havertz scoring the decisive goal to give Mikel Arteta’s side their first Premier League victory at Anfield since 2012.

Following the match, Arsenal defender Jurrien Timber shared a photograph on Instagram showing him involved in a heated exchange with Liverpool midfielder Alexis Mac Allister.

Timber accompanied the picture with the caption: “Proud of the team! Enjoy this one, Gooners.”

Liverpool fans were quick to notice that Gravenberch had appeared to like the post, prompting an angry reaction on social media.

Some supporters questioned the midfielder’s loyalty, with others suggesting he should be sold or disciplined by the club.

Gravenberch, 24, was an unused substitute during Liverpool’s defeat. He and Timber are close friends, having played together at Ajax for two years before continuing their relationship as team-mates with the Netherlands national side.

It is not clear whether Gravenberch personally liked the post or whether the interaction was made by someone managing his social media account.

The incident has nevertheless caused frustration among sections of the Liverpool support following a disappointing result against their Premier League rivals.

#1782. Messi was a deity among Argentina’s unholy rabble

Little sorcerer calls time on playing for his country six weeks after World Cup final defeat which was marred by brutality of his team-mates

Oliver Brown leads coverage of the greatest events in sport all over the world. He has reported on multiple Olympic Games, World Cups, Ashes series and Super Bowls, plus all major golf and tennis tournaments. His awards include Sports Feature Writer of the Year and Sports Interviewer of the Year. He was named Sports Journalist of the Year in 2024 by the London Press Club. His awards include Sports Feature Writer of the Year and Sports Interviewer of the Year. He was named Sports Journalist of the Year in 2024 by the London Press Club. Lionel Messi’s haunted expression told you more than a three-page retirement statement, artfully displayed alongside a golden pen, ever could. Sobbing and desolate under a cloudless New Jersey sky, he understood that his last game for Argentina had also been among his worst.

Where four years earlier he had adorned the greatest World Cup final with two goals, he found no artistry to salvage this abomination of an encore, drifting into anonymity while his team-mates triggered a bare-knuckle brawl. No wonder he stood apart while Leandro Paredes and Nahuel Molina did their worst, preferring to absorb one more chorus of adoration from the blue-and-white disciples before forsaking the stage for good.

You could make the case that Messi, as captain of an unholy rabble that had sought only to kick lumps out of Spain, should have taken a moral lead by hauling his team-mates into line, rather than reducing himself to their level by agitating to have Marc Cucurella sent off.

And yet for 20 years, the little sorcerer stayed aloof from his nation’s most lurid antics on the pitch, establishing himself as a strangely beatific presence on whom the highest ideals could be projected. Anybody who has heard Messi’s name being chanted by 50,000 fervent Argentines would have felt it. He was as close as 21st-century sport has come to a secular deity, the object of such veneration that Pope Francis felt compelled to remind Catholics that it was sacrilegious to keep calling him God.

Today, with one agonised announcement, that glorious delirium is over, and already Argentina seems not to know what to do with itself. Pablo Giralt, a sports anchor in Buenos Aires, was unable even to speak when he heard the news live on air, while shattered young fans described how they had called their parents in tears.

Everybody had known the moment was approaching, given the finality of his exit from the final and the subsequent death of his father, Jorge, but it still triggered an unbearable sense of loss.

Messi was the force who galvanised a nation, propelling his side from the unfathomable low of defeat to Saudi Arabia at the 2022 World Cup to holding the trophy aloft 26 days later. Who could ever hope to emulate him, to detonate such joy that the team’s homecoming bus parade in the capital had to be abandoned for a helicopter ride because of the millions on the streets?

“Thank you, God, for making me Argentine,” Messi wrote in his earnest sign-off, his strength of allegiance unfailing to the end. As a veteran of 207 international matches, with his last at La Bombonera distinguished by an ecstatic ovation, he understood both the passions he unleashed among his people and the extent to which his own story became that of an entire country.

You struggled to imagine what life was like in the eye of this madness, with his every move stalked. For the wonder of Messi was that the cult went beyond borders, that the joy he inspired across six World Cups made him beloved to billions. An abiding memory of the 2022 final is of the walk back to the metro station in Doha, where thousands of Nepalese and Bangladeshi supporters, all part of the vast migrant workforce that had built the stadiums, united in “Messi, Messi” refrains even at 1am.

Messi was majestic at that tournament, so imperious in filleting Croatia in the semi-finals that Argentina’s TV reporters abandoned even the pretence of objectivity. “Truly, you made your mark in everyone’s life, and that to me is beyond winning any World Cup,” gushed Sofia Martinez of Television Publica. And when he won it all, the mark only deepened. To occupy any press box at the World Cup where Argentina were involved this summer was to see South American colleagues in “Messi 10” jerseys, helplessly in thrall to his greatness.

As a 39-year-old, he confounded every expectation, scoring a hat-trick against Algeria and breaking Miroslav Klose’s World Cup goals record. Even when engineering those implausible fightbacks against Egypt and England, he held a volatile team together with a minimum of fuss.

Lionel Messi: #FIFAWorldCup edition 🇦🇷🌟 pic.twitter.com/E2xOh3Iose

To study Messi at his last World Cup was to see a man spared the obligation to do anything off the ball. For large periods of each game, the most minutely scrutinised athlete on the planet would do little besides wander around, only to ignite when it mattered most. You saw it in the fateful semi-final with England, where, at 1-0 down, he sloped off to the right touchline as if absent-mindedly gardening. Except he was plotting his opponents’ downfall, working out the precise spots from which to unleash two sumptuous crosses and shatter English hearts.

That alchemy would elude him in the final, where Argentina’s bid for immortality brought only instant notoriety, not to mention £236,000 in fines for misconduct. Was Messi’s image hurt by his connection to the chaos? Not in the long run. Nobody likes to cling to the fact that Pelé’s swansong for Brazil was a drawn friendly with Yugoslavia, or that Diego Maradona bowed out of World Cup football by failing a drug test for ephedrine. What endure are the indelible masterpieces those players bequeathed en route.

It will be the same for Messi, a genius defined less by his ending than by the electrifying adrenalin rush he produced along the way, spanning three finals, 21 goals, and countless flourishes to take the breath away. “Thank you” was all he had left to say. And yet the gratitude, ultimately, is all ours.

#1781. McGinn insists Villa are ‘under no illusions’ ahead of Barcelona test

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

John McGinn insisted Aston Villa are "under no illusions" and will only enjoy their trip to Barcelona if they beat Hansi Flick's side.

Villa face Barca at Camp Nou on Tuesday, looking to extend their perfect start in the Champions League this season.

Last season's Europa League winners have defeated Club Brugge, Fenerbahce and Viking in UEFA's premier competition this term, leaving them second in the league phase.

Villa have led for more minutes than any other team in the Champions League this season (240:09), while they are one of only three teams yet to trail at any point, along with Paris Saint-Germain and Stuttgart.

Villa will face Barca for the first time since January 1983, when the English side won the Super Cup 3-1 on aggregate, and McGinn is seeking a famous win against the European giants.

"You always want to face new teams, new experiences, not only for players to test yourselves, but for supporters to experience it as well," said McGinn.

Camp Nou. Champions League. Aston Villa. https://t.co/4hkHq1OUMI

— Aston Villa (@AstonVilla) November 2, 2026

"I was looking for Barcelona or Real Madrid away and we managed to get Barca, so it's a great draw, but obviously we're under no illusions.

"It's only going to be an enjoyable experience if we can come away with the three points, so we’re all excited and looking forward to it.

"We're no different to anyone else in football that really looks forward to playing there and pitting themselves against one of the best teams in the world, so we're really excited, but focused on the task ahead.

"Obviously, a very special game, but once you get over that fact that you're playing Barcelona away, we're going over there to put a performance in and carry on what has been an unbelievable start in the Champions League."

The four previous meetings between Barca and Villa came between 1978 and 1983 – after going unbeaten in the first three (W2 D1), the Blaugrana were beaten in the fourth (3-0 in the Super Cup final second leg).

Villa boss Unai Emery has faced Barca on 30 occasions in his managerial career, winning just three of those (D6 L21). Of the teams he has faced 5+ times, his win percentage against Barca is his lowest against any opponent (10%).

#1780. Aston Villa make legal action decision after Jamie Carragher apology

Aston Villa have decided against taking legal action against Sky Sports pundit Jamie Carragher.

The club had threatened legal proceedings against the former England defender after he made "unacceptable insults" on the Stick To Football podcast last week.

Carragher told Villa supporters to "shut the f*** up" after facing criticism for suggesting Unai Emery should consider taking the Manchester United job if Michael Carrick is sacked.

The pundit apologised on social media, admitting his language was "clumsy and wrong".

Villa will take no further action, the Press Association reports.

Owner Nassef Sawiris said in a statement on Friday: "Aston Villa will initiate legal action against Jamie Carragher for his unacceptable insults about the Club and its fans.

"Aston Villa will not allow anyone to stop our ascension in English and European football."

Carragher quickly apologised, insisting his comments were "tongue in cheek".

He posted on social media: "I’d like to apologise to Aston Villa, the owners and their fans.

"My language this week was clumsy and wrong.

"I can assure Villa fans it was tongue in cheek but I can understand it’s not come across that way, so apologies."

Villa return to Champions League action on Tuesday when they take on Barcelona at the Nou Camp.

#1779. Michael Olise vs. Eberechi Eze: How two Palace standouts took such different paths at Arsenal and Bayern Munich

By Axel Clody | 02 Nov 2026 13:55

The Frenchman has become the creative reference point for the Bavarian giants, while the Englishman is still looking for his place at Arsenal.

Michael Olise and Eberechi Eze left Crystal Palace at different times, but they shared something: they had established themselves as two of the most talented players at the club. The Frenchman went to Bayern Munich in 2024, while the Englishman fulfilled his dream of playing for Arsenal a year later.

Since then, their trajectories have taken different directions, showing how tactical context and space within a team can be decisive for a player’s development.

Olise turned the potential he showed in England into a leading role in Germany. Since arriving at Bayern Munich, the attacker has become one of the team’s main offensive creators, combining goals, assists and constant involvement in build-up play. Ninth place in the 2026 Ballon d’Or recognised an evolution that was already evident on the pitch, although a higher position would have been fairer.

Eze, on the other hand, has not yet been able to reproduce the influence he had at Palace at Arsenal. Signed to add creativity and the ability to unbalance the attack, the midfielder alternates between performances out wide and opportunities as an alternative to Martin Odegaard. The change of role, together with the competition for places, helps explain why his adaptation is far from achieving the same success as his former team-mate.

Michael Olise’s numbers in Germany show a progression that goes beyond a good run in front of goal. In his first season at Bayern Munich, in 2024-25, the Frenchman scored 20 goals and provided 20 assists in 55 games. The following campaign, he maintained his consistency and raised his output to 21 goals and 26 assists in 52 games. At the start of 2026-27, he already has 10 goals and five assists in just 11 appearances.

The number of direct goal contributions is striking, but it does not explain the attacker’s importance on its own. Olise is a player capable of taking responsibility for finishing a move or identifying the team-mate in a better position to finish it. His repertoire includes passes that break defensive lines, accurate crosses, combinations in tight spaces and individual moves that force opponents to shift their marking.

That variety makes him a true playmaker, even when playing mainly on the flanks.

Olise does not need to receive the ball in a position to shoot to be decisive: he can also drop back a few metres, take part in circulation and speed up the attack with a pass that disorganises the defence. When he finds space to carry the ball towards the box, he adds a constant goal threat to that creative ability.

Bayern Munich’s context also favours this repertoire. In a team that often takes control of matches and has attackers capable of getting into the box, Olise finds options to turn his vision into assists. The presence of team-mates who move to receive his passes widens the possibilities for combinations and prevents opposition marking from focusing exclusively on blocking his shots.

That does not mean the Frenchman has become a different player from the one at Crystal Palace. In England, he already showed technical quality, vision and the ability to decide matches. The difference is in the dimension those characteristics have reached in Munich.

Bayern Munich offers a bigger stage, but Olise has also risen to the demands, improving his consistency and his ability to influence different moments of matches.

Eberechi Eze’s trajectory is more complex because his difficulty is not limited to attacking production. In 2024-25, his last full season at Crystal Palace, the midfielder scored 15 goals and provided 11 assists in 43 games. He was one of the main sources of the team’s creativity, with the freedom to receive between the lines, carry the ball and get close to the box. His performances justified Arsenal’s interest, and they signed him in 2025.

His first season at Arsenal, however, left a less impressive record than the raw numbers may suggest. Eze scored 10 goals and provided five assists in 52 games in 2025-26.

They are reasonable statistics for a player who had to adapt to a new team, but the distribution of the goals deserves attention: five of them came in just two north London derbies against Tottenham, both in the Premier League. In one of those games he scored a hat-trick, in the other he found the net twice.

Those two games helped build his image as a tormentor of Tottenham, but they also show why the total goal count is not enough to judge his season. Outside those matches, Eze was unable to maintain a frequency of decisive contributions that would put him among Arsenal’s main attacking references.

The problem is not to disregard the importance of scoring in derbies, but to recognise that one-off great performances do not replace the constant influence expected of a player signed to add creativity to the team.

The tactical question is central. At Palace, Eze played in a system with three centre-backs and two wing-backs, the 3-4-3, which allowed him to occupy inside areas often and take part directly in creation. At Arsenal, his use has been more variable. In some games he appears out wide; in others he appears as an alternative to Odegaard, who occupies an important central role in the team’s offensive organisation.

The difference is not only in the starting position. When he receives further from the box, Eze has to beat his marker in situations where he has fewer passing options nearby. Inside, he can make better use of his carrying, his ability to turn under pressure and his vision to find team-mates. At the same time, competing with Odegaard means competing for a position in which Arsenal already have an established player in the collective structure.

The start of 2026-27 reinforces the difficulty of gaining continuity. Eze has two goals and one assist in 12 games in all competitions. In the first eight Premier League rounds, he started only twice, came on from the bench in another four and did not leave the bench in the other two. With fewer minutes and alternating roles, it is harder to gain rhythm, build understanding and establish a run of performances capable of changing his situation.

The comparison with Olise, therefore, should not be read as a definitive verdict on Eze’s quality. The two arrived at their new clubs in different circumstances and found different demands. The Frenchman gained space to turn his creativity into a central weapon for Bayern Munich; the Englishman still needs to find a role in which he can take more part in build-up and receive the ball in the zones where he performs best.

The talent that made Eze one of Palace’s standouts has not disappeared. The question is how to use it in an Arsenal side with an offensive structure different from the one he was used to. Olise has already found that answer at Bayern Munich and become one of the team’s most influential names. Eze is still looking for his, and until he wins space and consistency, the gap between the two trajectories is likely to remain evident.

#1778. Michael Carrick reveals Manchester United injury latest as Patrick Dorgu makes surprise return

Michael Carrick has confirmed that Patrick Dorgu will not feature for Manchester United against Roma.

The winger returned to team training after an extended lay-off with a hamstring injury that he picked up on international duty in September.

It left the Red Devils without one of their senior left-back options, and that has led them to be short in that position after Luke Shaw’s muscle injury which has also kept the England international out.

Dorgu’s comeback is a big boost to under-fire head coach Carrick, who has overseen a nine-game winless run which has piled on the pressure on the former midfielder.

However, the Dane will not play any part as United return to continental competition tomorrow.

"It was his first day with the group, great to have him back, but he won't be involved tomorrow,” Carrick told the media. “We'll see how he progresses for the week [ahead]."

The sack looked as though it was looming after 4-1 and 3-0 thrashings by Como and Bournemouth respectively, but he was retained by the club’s hierarchy ahead of the trip to Chelsea last weeknend.

United were beaten once more by the Blues, with Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer scoring for the hosts as Lisandro Martinez was sent off for the visitors, who slid to 17th in the Premier League table.

Carrick was also asked about Martinez’s mindset after the Argentine’s red card, which followed on from his stunning TV interview in the wake of the defeat by Atletico Madrid last month.

“I've got no concerns about commitment at all,” the head coach continued.

“Things happen in football, sometimes you make mistakes, sometimes it goes well for you, but commitment is not an issue, for sure."

#1776. Man Utd need a Mikel Arteta in charge - but club's rotten core means any manager is a dead man walking

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

There are a couple of signs that a Premier League manager at one of the traditional top clubs is fearing for his job.

One, obviously, is an extended poor run of results. The second is the 'Mikel Arteta Got Time And Look At Arsenal Now' card gets whipped out. It has never been played from a position of strength.

The idea that Arteta's tenure at Arsenal is something of a blueprint has been regularly latched onto by those at rival clubs, the suggestion being that time and time alone is the answer to all problems.

When his time in the Tottenham dugout was stumbling to an early conclusion, Thomas Frank pointed hopefully across north London.

“I think it is a good example of a club that sticks to the process," Frank said.

“It took probably three seasons for Arteta, so the fourth season, that is where he competed. Now he is in the seventh season. So he is really, really ready to compete in his fourth season."

There was nothing in Frank's tenure to suggest he deserved to make it that far. No bold, ambitious thinking. No long-term vision to persuade supporters or the club's hierarchy that short-term pain was worth enduring.

His authority was consistently eroded. Frank disciplined Yves Bissouma, a player already heading for the exit door, for lateness, but dissent from Cristian Romero, Djed Spence and Micky van de Ven all later went unpunished.

Michael Carrick is the latest to use Arteta as something of a shield in an attempt to cling onto his Manchester United job, despite the best efforts of his players.

"It pains me to say, but the one that won the league in our country last season has been there for a long period of time," Carrick said last month.

"It’s seven years, and the first two seasons [they finished] maybe eighth or seventh."

Whether they were given seven months, seven years, or seven decades, most managers would not have turned around the mess that Arsenal were in when Arteta took charge.

Carrick reveals Man Utd injury latest after surprise return

Transfer news LIVE: Arsenal eye Brazil star; Man Utd in Barcelona swap

Gravenberch angers Liverpool fans with Timber interaction

Rediscover your adventurous side on an exotic getaway

The desperation for results is prioritised over addressing Manchester United’s rotten core

The Spaniard possesses a unique character, an aura that brings people along with him. It was that intensity and force of character that persuaded Arsenal to take a punt on him. Within a year, he was promoted from head coach to manager. What has followed since is testament to the extraordinary leader he is.

Crucially, Arteta had people above him willing to go all in. He wanted decisive action and Arsenal backed him.

Henrikh Mkhitaryan had his contract terminated barely six months into Arteta’s reign. Mesut Ozil, the club's highest-paid player, was cast aside and had his deal torn up in the Spaniard’s first full season in charge. Sokratis and Shkodran Mustafi followed almost immediately in similarly ruthless exits.

Arsenal needed a cultural reset. Arteta had the personality to demand that but also the authority to enact it. Club captain Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang was stripped of his duties for repeatedly being late and ultimately had his contract ripped up as well.

The impact? Mohammed Elneny said in 2022: "Everyone is scared with their position because this happened to Aubameyang.

"Of course if anyone is not the captain of the team, does a small mistake, they are going to have the same problem, and no one needs that problem."

Arsenal's hierarchy could very easily have sided with Aubameyang or Ozil, both on £350,000-a-week, over Arteta. That would have been less embarrassing from an optics and a financial perspective. Instead, a line was drawn in the sand.

Player power would not usurp Arteta's authority. Everything since then, from the harmonious dressing room to the connection with the fans, from the extraordinary work-rate of his players to the pride in defending the cause, has been built on those foundations.

Time will not help Carrick at United when he has been given no other tools. Lisandro Martinez, who should have been moved on a long time ago, slagged off the club's executives but was not dropped. Two matches later, he displayed remarkable stupidity in being sent off against Chelsea.

Bruno Fernandes, the club captain, took aim at Carrick himself. He sat out for one match but then returned with the armband still in his possession. The desperation for results was prioritised over addressing the club's rotten core.

The same players will get another manager sacked. Results will pick up and optimism will briefly return, but the underlying issues will remain. Nothing fundamentally will have changed.

It is easy to throw out buzzwords like patience and process, just as it is easy to allow a manager to limp on towards an inevitable conclusion, hoping to hide from deeper failings and another major decision the hierarchy got wrong.

Clubs want to believe in the Arteta model without signing up to the pain that comes with it. That is a blueprint, but only for further decline.

#1775. Michael Carrick makes 'crazy' admission as Manchester United delay sack decision

Michael Carrick does not feel like his time as Manchester United manager is running out.

The under-fire head coach has overseen a run of nine straight games without a victory this term, and his United side sit 17th in the Premier League after their worst start to a campaign in 40 years.

The Red Devils have won just once in the league all season, with their other victory coming in the Champions League against minnows Sabah.

On the continent, they were handed hefty defeats by Atletico Madrid and Como, with the latter resulting in Carrick apologising to the travelling supporters, raising his hands in acknowledgement.

The writing seemed to be on the wall for the former midfielder after a heavy 3-0 demolition at home by Bournemouth, who ran riot at a tempestuous Old Trafford.

It seemed as though Carrick was waving goodbye to the United fans as he walked off the pitch, and the home faithful turned on the players with relentless booing at the full-time whistle as they trudged off.

United were beaten again last weekend as Chelsea secured a 2-0 win at Stamford Bridge, with Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer on the scoresheet for Xabi Alonso’s Blues.

Lisandro Martinez, who hit the headline for his open criticism of the club’s hierarchy following the loss at Atletico Madrid in October, was sent off in west London and Carrick did not acknowledge the centre-back as he made his way back to the dressing room.

Despite all that, Carrick does not feel like he is a “coach with two games left”, after it was reported that the club had spared him the sack, seeking to reassess his position during the November international break.

“You you never know what is going to happen in the future, but that doesn't change the way I feel. I can't wait for the agme tomorrow. You might think I'm crazy with the results we've had, but I can't wait for it."

United take on Roma in the Champions League on Tuesday before a home encounter with Aston Villa at the weekend.

Manchester United will not be able to welcome back Patrick Dorgu when they take on Roma this evening.

There had been a hope that the Dane could slot back in to solve the Red Devils’ left-back problems after the versatile winger returned to team training on Monday.

Michael Carrick, the under-fire head coach, confirmed to the media that while the former Lecce man had made a comeback, he would not be involved in the Champions League tie.

"It was his first day with the group, great to have him back, but he won't be involved tomorrow,” Carrick said. “We'll see how he progresses for the week [ahead]."

As such, it means that United are once again hamstrung in that position, with Luke Shaw also sidelined with a muscle problem.

Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui have deputised from right-back in recent matches, with central defender Leny Yoro coming in as a makeshift right-sided full-back. Ayden Heaven is also an option in that position.

Further forward, the Red Devils are still without Marcus Rashford, who remains sidelined with a niggling hip issue that kept him out of the heavy defeats by Como and Bournemouth, while he was not fit enough to face Chelsea either. He has not since returned to training, and will not feature here.

Benjamin Sesko is a longer-term absentee as the Slovenian continues his recovery from a shin problem that curtailed his debut campaign and stunted his start to this season.

It therefore leaves Carrick relatively short of options for the visit of Roma, but he will have Kobbie Mainoo to call upon in the engine room after the academy graduate returned to training ahead of the trip to Chelsea, and he was introduced as a substitute at Stamford Bridge.

The England international could well come into the starting lineup here, although it remains to be seen who could join him in centre-field.

With the pressure on Sage’s shoulders starting to reach a boiling point, Crystal Palace are desperately searching for a much-welcomed Europa League boost here. Watching Hoffenheim lose five of their previous six showdowns away from the SNP Arena across all competitions, Palace will be eager to kickstart their campaign. #1772. Man United head coach Michael Carrick addresses fresh speculation surrounding his future ahead of fascinating Roma showdown

By Matt Law | 02 Nov 2026 14:00, Last updated: 02 Nov 2026 14:03

Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick has said that he "can't wait" for Tuesday's Champions League clash with Roma at Old Trafford.

The Red Devils are without a victory in their last nine matches in all competitions, and there is major pressure on Carrick during an incredibly difficult period for the club.

Man United have lost four of their last five matches, including each of their last three, but Carrick is still convinced that he is the right man for the job.

The 20-time English champions will play two more fixtures ahead of the November international break, hosting Roma in Europe, before welcoming Aston Villa to Old Trafford in the Premier League this weekend.

When asked whether he feels as if he has only two more games at the helm, Carrick said: "No, not at all. You you never know what is going to happen in the future, but that doesn't change the way I feel.

"I can't wait for the game tomorrow. You might think I'm crazy with the results we've had, but I can't wait for it.

"The dressing room is in a good place. Perception is a funny thing, you can make things look in different ways. The commitment from the players, to the club and each other, I don't question that at all.

"It's what I am, it's what I live for, a lot of people could do my job when you're winning games. It hasn't changed my mindset (bad results)."

Carrick had been widely expected to lose his job off the back of Man United's 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth in the Premier League on October 25.

The Englishman led the Red Devils into Saturday's game at Chelsea, and while it was a much-improved performance, Man United lost again.

The 20-time English champions will play five times in November, facing Liverpool in their first match after the upcoming international break, before tackling Sporting Lisbon and Brentford.

Eddie Howe remains the favourite to replace Carrick at the helm, should Man United make a change in the dug-out.

#1771. “I can’t change it” – Chivu looks back after three derby defeats to Milan

After last night’s win against Inter, AC Milan have now gone eight games without a defeat in the Derby della Madonnina.

In years gone by, the derby was a result to skip over for Milan. It was a defeat waiting to happen and it seemingly couldn’t be changed and then it flipped. Matteo Gabbia’s goal stopped the streak and in turn, it started a new one.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The Rossoneri entered last night’s game with a run of seven unbeaten and they finished the night with eight unbeaten and a fourth consecutive win. It’s a first in itself for more than 50 years, which is telling.

It’s a result which brought Gerry Cardinale to tears and it’s clear that something has really clicked at San Siro, as the player ratings showed.

Speaking at a press conference after the game, as relayed by MilanNews, the Inter coach spoke about several things, including his unfavourable record in the Derby della Madonnina.

“Compared to last year, there’s something to note about our approach to matches: the superficiality and casualness with which we handle certain situations, where we lack a bit of grit, a bit of determination, a bit of danger perception. But we need to rediscover them.

“We need to be aware that right now, despite a few more points than last year, we’ve lost something that absolutely needs to be rediscovered.”

“I couldn’t, because the forwards have had some problems in the last few days. Bonny only made himself available on the last day after two days with a fever of 39°C and severe nausea and vomiting, so we were forced to find a solution, to make a virtue of necessity, changing the system a bit.

“We knew that, in this type of match, it would be the right thing to have pace on the wings with Spence and Carlos and attack the line a bit more, as well as looking for depth in space with Diouf operating under the striker, looking for both him and Sucic between the lines.

“Unfortunately, sometimes things don’t work out, but, I repeat, we were forced to change.”

“It’s too easy to talk now that Lautaro is injured and the other two forwards aren’t feeling well. These things happen, fortunately not often. We’ll make some assessments, but we’re still happy with our four forwards, in addition to what Lavelli gives us, what Mosconi gives us, and whoever we bring in from the Under 23s.

“But, I repeat, it’s too easy to bring these things up at a time when two forwards aren’t at their best and the third is injured.”

Is there something mental that comes into play in the derby?

“There’s always something mental, I think, and history teaches us this, when you get to play another season after winning.

“So, let’s try not to throw everything away and try to rediscover some determination, some humility in doing certain things, starting with myself, because I’m primarily responsible for everything we do.

“We shouldn’t throw everything away because we’ve reached the tenth matchday and this is the first game we’ve lost. We’ve got 25 points, and last year we’d got fewer, but we’ve always been able to react, we’ve always kept our feet on the ground and our heads down to build a strong season.

“That’s what we’d like to do again this year, because we have this desire and this ambition to have another strong season; we just need to find the way to build it again.”

#1768. Pierre Sage makes sack admission as Crystal Palace future hangs in balance after Tottenham defeat

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Pierre Sage has called on Crystal Palace supporters to trust him, but admits his future is not in his hands after their 2-0 defeat to Tottenham.

Palace were comfortbaly beaten at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, with goals from Archie Gray and Jan Paul van Hecke ensuring Spurs took advantage of Jean-Philippe Mateta’s early red card.

Sage is under increasing pressure to turn things around, with Palace mired in the relegation zone after winning one of their first nine league games, but he insists he will continue to fight for his future.

Asked if he was aware of the Eagles’ league position, Sage cut a defiant tone but added it was not up to him whether he kept his job.

“I am really aware of the situation,” Sage said.

“I don’t like this situation. [But] you can trust in me, I will never give up. I want to be the first on the pitch on Monday. I have the rage to train more. It’s not me to decide this thing [my future]. If I have one hour, I will give my best for one hour. If I have ten years, I will give my best for ten years.”

Relegation fears are deepening for Palace, and Sage acknowledges that dropping down to the Championship would be a disaster for the club after their third successive defeat in the league.

"Yes, [relegation], it’s a disaster for every club in the Premier League and especially that I have to speak about my club. You know I’m not comfortable with the situation in the table, but it’s a consequence of what we did bad on the pitch,” the Frenchman continued.

“My only action is on the team and on the pitch. That is why I can speak about the situation of the club in the table, of my situation, because it’s a consequence to of this, but my only way to change a thing is to go on the pitch. That is why I talk to the players and I want to be the first on the pitch on Monday. They can trust in me.

“I will never give up. I will do the best session I can do on Monday because now I have the rage to train more because the game I saw was not in line with my conviction.

“I don’t like when we let the initiative too much to the opponent. I was really impressed by what I see of the other team, and I like this kind of play. I know we are not the same team, but we are able to do things with the ball, and we have to improve that."

#1767. Blackburn Rovers vs Stoke City - prediction, team news, lineups

By Calum Burrowes | 02 Nov 2026 14:12, Last updated: 02 Nov 2026 17:02

After facing Welsh opposition in successive weekends, Blackburn Rovers will be looking to return to winning ways in the Championship on Tuesday night when they welcome in-form Stoke City to Ewood Park.

Rovers were thrashed by high-flying Swansea City in South Wales at the weekend and will be eager to put that 4-0 defeat behind them, while the Potters returned to winning ways after a goalless draw with Bristol City by beating Preston North End 2-0 to round off a successful October in style.

Having narrowly avoided relegation to League One last season, Blackburn Rovers turned to former manager Tony Mowbray in the summer, hoping the 62-year-old could guide the Lancashire club further up the table.

After 13 Championship matches back at the club where he oversaw 267 games between February 2017 and May 2022, Mowbray has made a positive start, with five wins, three draws and five defeats leaving Rovers 13th in the table and nine points clear of the relegation zone.

Blackburn have faced all three Welsh sides in the Championship this month, with victories over Cardiff City and Wrexham helping them move further away from danger, but a heavy 4-0 defeat to promotion hopefuls Swansea on Saturday prevented them from making it three such wins in a row.

Mowbray's side travelled across the border just two points outside the top eight, having won four of their previous six league outings, but goals from Stephen Eustaquio, Joseph Opoku and Filip Lissah in the first half, followed by Ross Stewart's strike shortly before the hour mark, condemned Rovers to their heaviest defeat of the campaign.

A victory on Tuesday against a side they have failed to beat in their last four meetings could leave Blackburn just one point outside the playoff places heading into the weekend, underlining the progress they have made after finishing 20th and only five points above the bottom three last season.

As for Stoke City, they make the 70-mile journey north looking to build on an excellent start to the campaign, having defied expectations after ending last season in the bottom half of the table.

Under Mark Robins, the Potters have made their best start to a Championship season since being relegated from the Premier League in 2018, collecting seven wins, two draws and four defeats from their opening 13 matches to sit seventh with 23 points.

Stoke began the 2026-27 campaign with three successive defeats but have since turned their fortunes around following a 4-1 thrashing by Wolverhampton Wanderers at the end of August.

A change in formation, with Robins now favouring a back three, has helped spark an impressive run of seven wins in their last 10 matches, with their only defeat during that period coming against league leaders Middlesbrough, who snatched a 91st-minute winner.

Since the start of September, no side has conceded fewer goals than Robins' men, highlighting the impact of their reshaped young defence at the bet365 Stadium, while a 2-0 victory over bottom club Preston North End at the weekend was secured through goals from Ben Wilmot and Jack McGlynn.

The sides meet for the first time this season, having drawn 1-1 in each of their last two encounters.

Following a 4-0 defeat last time out, Mowbray may have been considering changes regardless, but further injury problems mean he will have little choice but to freshen up his side for Tuesday's clash.

Harry Pickering was forced off after just 24 minutes against Swansea and will miss this match, with Gady Beyuku having replaced him at the time and now in contention to start against the Potters.

The full-back will join Adam Forshaw and Ryoya Morishita on the sidelines, although the midfield duo are closing in on returns to action.

On a more positive note, Yuri Ribeiro and Yuki Ohashi are both be available for selection after returning to the bench last time out, having missed the previous month and eight weeks respectively.

As for the visitors, Robins has the option of naming an unchanged side, although the quick turnaround between fixtures could prompt some alterations.

Stoke will be without Eric Bocat, Ato Ampah, Sam Gallagher and Lamine Cisse, but captain Viktor Johansson is expected to retain his place in goal, while American winger McGlynn is also likely to feature after netting for the third time in the league on Saturday.

Blackburn Rovers possible starting lineup:

B. Toth; Alebiosu, Atcheson, McLoughlin, Pickering; Baradji, Montgomery; Fevrier, Cantwell; Afolayan; Gudjohnsen

Johansson; Wilmot, Lawal, Graham; Johnson, Soumare, Galbraith, Bombino; McGlynn, Bozenik, Devenny

Although both sides have made far more encouraging starts to the new season than many of their supporters might have anticipated, we expect Stoke to come away from Ewood Park with all three points on Tuesday night.

The Potters will be keen to extend their unbeaten run to four matches, and we believe they can do so by claiming an eighth league victory of the campaign and moving closer to the automatic promotion places.

#1766. Prediction: AZ Alkmaar vs Juventus

Looking to lay down a Europa League marker on Thursday night, Juventus will travel to the Netherlands when they meet AZ Alkmaar.

With a stacked midweek schedule from across the continent, there are plenty of eye-catching Europa League betting promotions available.

Ahead of Thursday’s showdown from the AFAS Stadion, you can find all of the key AZ Alkmaar vs Juventus H2H stats here.

Starting with the hosts, while AZ Alkmaar might have enjoyed a dominant start to proceedings when opening up the 2026/27 campaign, Lee-Roy Echteld’s men are desperately searching for some recent stability. Last seen over the weekend putting in a toothless display as they were hit with a 1-0 loss away at Dutch giants Ajax, the Cheese Farmers have come under some scrutiny over the past few weeks. Hit with consecutive Eredivisie defeats for the first time this season, Alkmaar have also registered just a sole win from any of their previous four appearances across all competitions. Facing what is a blockbuster Europa League showdown on Thursday night, the Reds are also searching for some much-welcomed defensive grit. In fact, the one-time PSG coach has seen his inconsistent squad muster just a single clean sheet from their last six straight attempts.

All still dealing with respective injury issues, AZ Alkmaar will be unable to call upon the trio of Jizz Hornkamp, Kees Smit and summer recruit Stije Resink. However, despite currently serving a domestic suspension, former Sparta Rotterdam youngster Ayoub Oufkir will return to Echteld’s squad here.

Settling for a spot on the bench away at Ajax on Saturday, ex-Watford defender Wesley Hoedt could be handed an immediate full recall. Notching a pair of Europa League strikes in his first three group stage appearances, Dutch marksman Mexx Meerdink will lead Alkmaar’s attack.

As for the visitors, while Juventus might have made an immediate return to winning ways last time out as they secured a stellar 2-0 victory at home against bitter domestic foes Napoli, the Old Lady will be dreaming of a repeat performance here. However, missing out on what they had billed as a golden opportunity on October 22nd as they were eventually forced to settle for a 2-2 stalemate against French outfit Rennes, Luciano Spalletti’s side are also searching for some essential stability. Coming under plenty of scrutiny last month as they slumped to an infamous 3-0 drumming at the hands of Lazio, Juventus have failed to register back-to-back wins since the middle of September. Widely regarded as a standout Europa League title contender this season, the Old Lady will be hoping to make a real statement on foreign soil in midweek.

Juggling what has become a stacked injury list in Turin, Juventus will once again be without the likes of Zeki Celik, Franciso Conceicao, Kennan Yildiz and French international Khephren Thuram here. Likewise, dealing with a recent calf issue, ex-Fiorentina star Nicolas Gonzalez remains a major doubt.

Coming off the bench and bagging a maiden Serie A strike of the season against Napoli last weekend, Jeremie Boga could be handed a full recall. Arriving from Tottenham on a year-long loan switch, Guglielmo Vicario will start between the sticks.

Making an immediate return to winning ways last time out as they clinched a 2-0 victory at home against bitter domestic rivals Napoli, Juventus will be dreaming of a repeat performance when they turn their attention back to Europa League action in midweek. Mustering seven points from their opening three group stage showdowns, the Italian icons are desperate to make a public statement on foreign soil. However, with AZ Alkmaar drawing back-to-back blanks for the first time so far this calendar year, don’t be surprised to see a nail-biting affair on Thursday night.
