#1745. Man City sign Enzo Fernandez for £125m to end transfer saga of the summer

Manchester City have equalled the British record transfer on deadline day after agreeing to pay £125m to sign midfielder Enzo Fernández from Chelsea.

The deal brings to an end the biggest saga of the summer and means that Enzo Maresca, the new City head coach, has landed his number one target.

City left it until the last day of the transfer window to strike an agreement after Chelsea decided that Fernández’s exit was in the best interests of the club. But a late move to replace the Argentine with Monaco midfielder Lamie Camara collapsed to the anger of the Premier League club, leaving Xabi Alonso one player light among his midfield options.

Having refused to meet Chelsea’s self-imposed deadline to sign Fernández for £120m earlier in the summer, City had to equal the £125m Liverpool paid Newcastle United for Alexander Isak 12 months earlier.

Fernández had made it clear that he wanted to leave Chelsea some time ago and was left out of Alonso’s squad for the victories last week over Luton Town, in the Carabao Cup, and Brighton.

Having initially wanted to join Real Madrid, Fernández set his heart on linking back up with Maresca at City. The pair share a close relationship and had kept in touch after Maresca left Chelsea at the start of the year.

This is the second time Fernández has become the most expensive player in British transfer history, having previously set the record when he joined Chelsea for £107m from Benfica in the 2023 winter window.

Introducing our new Argentinian Blue 🇦🇷🩵 pic.twitter.com/nEHQ1oM855

During his time at Chelsea, 25-year-old Fernández won the Club World Cup and the Europa Conference League but he was also at the centre of controversy.

In January 2025, Fernández posted a video of himself and some of his Argentina international team-mates singing an offensive song about France players of African origin after winning the Copa America. He apologised to his Chelsea team-mates and made a donation to an anti-discrimination charity, but was still made the team’s vice-captain.

Last season was Fernández’s best goalscoring campaign, as he netted 15 goals in all competitions for Chelsea but the club finished 10th in the Premier League table. In April, he was suspended for two games by the club for suggesting he would like to live in Madrid – which was perceived as a come and get me plea to Real Madrid.

He angered England fans with his celebration after scoring against Thomas Tuchel’s team in Argentina’s World Cup semi-final victory over England, before being sent-off in the final defeat by Spain.

Chelsea fans booed Fernández in pre-season, although the club’s travelling supporters sang his name when he was introduced as a substitute in the victory over Fulham at the start of this season.

Fernández thanked his team-mates and the Chelsea staff in an emotional farewell post on Instagram. He added: “I want you to know that these have not been easy days for me. Writing this is not easy either. The truth is, I haven’t been in a good place.

“Three years ago, Cobham and Stamford Bridge became home for me and my family. I grew attached to the people, to the shirt, and to the badge of this incredible club.

“Believe me when I say that, from the moment I arrived, I became obsessed with winning and with bringing this club every trophy that its history deserves. We suffered, we cried, I got angry many times, but we also celebrated titles and unforgettable victories. Together, through the good times and the difficult ones.

“I live football the same way I live my life: with passion and with all my heart. That is why I want you to know that I understand you. I truly understand you, from the bottom of my heart.

“But life is about making decisions, and right now I find myself having to make one of those difficult decisions. I’ve said it before, but I want to say it again: I have grown incredibly fond of this club. Chelsea will always have a place in my thoughts and, above all, in my heart.

“But I also understand how football works. I know how passionate you are, because I am the same. And if I were in your position, I would probably be thinking the same way.”

Proper City 🤩🩵 pic.twitter.com/TfRTZOnPrw

The sale of Fernández means that Chelsea have set a new British transfer record of their own, having secured more than £500m in sales and loan fees during the summer transfer window.

Chelsea set about spending some of the money made from the Fernández sale by agreeing a last-minute deal for Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara.

Monaco had rejected a bid of £38.5m from Chelsea on deadline day, but an improved offer of £47m was accepted late on Tuesday night, only to be called off by Monaco on the stroke of the 11pm deadline.

Chelsea had been able to complete a medical during negotiations and Camara agreed to a six-year contract with the option of a further year to bolster Alonso’s midfield options, but he will now not join the club.

Chelsea had also seen at least one offer for Bournemouth’s Alex Scott rejected this summer, while the club showed an interest in Roma’s Manu Kone and explored whether or not a move for Arsenal’s Martin Zubimendi would be possible earlier this month.

Chilly tonight... pic.twitter.com/VihgKCScfn

The 21-year-old midfielder who came through the ranks at Real Madrid has been signed from Stuttgart.

Brighton’s sporting director Mike Cave said: “We’re delighted to welcome Chema to the club. He has an excellent pedigree having come through at Real Madrid; he followed that with a very good season with Stuttgart last season.

“We had been aware of Chema’s potential for sometime, and we are delighted to welcome him to the club, and look forward to working with him.”

Fernandez says: “Manchester City are the most successful club in England in recent times.

“Every player wants to be part of a club like this because everyone knows how well-run City are.

“I could not be happier to be here, and I am ready for the challenge of helping City continue winning trophies. This is a club built for success.

“If you look across the squad, City have quality in every area. I want to learn from my new teammates and become a better player.

Jack Grealish to Everton is done. A small gathering of fans are waiting outside Finch Farm, the club’s training base, but the calmness of this little road, will be at odds with the scrambling that is going on behind closed doors.

Zirkzee is staying at United. No move to Everton. United want the cover in attack and Everton’s approach happened too late with no chance of replacing him.

Crystal Palace have agreed a deal to re-sign Ben Chilwell. The 29-year-old was on loan at Palace last year and deal struck with Strasbourg for him to leave French club and return to the Premier League.

Sunderland were involved in the most bewildering transfer of the summer on deadline day as they fought a day-long tug-of-war with Crystal Palace for winger Malick Fofana.

On a day of claims and counterclaims, Sunderland have finally triumphed in the battle to land the Belgium international just an hour before the deadline.

But despite their success, it was a transfer that will leave a sour taste in the mouth to many, with the player repeatedly changing his mind about which club he wanted to join

As the saga dragged on, it is understood Fofana had a medical in Lyon with both Sunderland and Crystal Palace given access to the information as he still could not decide which club to join as talks continued into the evening.

Sunderland had a bid of around £25m accepted by Lyon on Tuesday morning and thought they had an agreement with both the player and his agent on personal terms and fees only for Palace to make a late attempt to hijack the deal.

The London club’s manager, Pierre Sage, who worked with Fofana at Lyon, is thought to have personally intervened in an attempt to persuade the player to move to South London. By late afternoon, Palace appeared to have got their man having also offered more money to Lyon and higher wages to the player and fees to his agency.

Sunderland, though, refused to concede defeat and, according to reports in France, launched a counter proposal of their own led by French owners Kyril Louis-Dreyfus who flew to Lyon to try and clinch the deal.

At one stage, it was even claimed that the player had two different private jets waiting at the airport to take him to either London or the North East depending on who he elected to sign for.

That was later refuted, although it is understood the player did have a medical in Lyon that could be viewed by both clubs before he made up his mind. That gave his representatives more time to thrash the terms of a deal with both clubs.

However, having failed to board an earlier flight to Lyon after talks with Palace advanced, Sunderland’s late push belatedly persuaded the 21-year-old to head to Wearside, and he is due to be unveiled on Wednesday morning.

Arsenal had also been linked with the player earlier this week but were not willing to match the asking price for Fofana who they viewed as a project player.

Mykhailo Mudryk’s loan move from Chelsea to Spurs has been confirmed.

Forgive the personal opinion but this is my favourite deal of the window. Mudryk played some of his best football under Roberto De Zerbi at Shakhtar Donetsk. The Spurs head coach has even described Mudryk as “my son”, and has previously tipped him as a future Ballon d’Or winner.

After so long out of the game, Mudryk now has a coach who knows exactly how to get the best out of him. It might not work at all. Mudryk may need months to rediscover his match sharpness after so long out. But I am very excited to find out.

Misha is Spurs 🇺🇦 pic.twitter.com/aW4VKFbvam

I think Chelsea come out of this deadline day very well. Sold a player who didn't want to play for them for a British record-equalling fee and signed a top target in double-quick time for a decent price in this market and in the circumstances. Strong window overall #cfc

Manuel Ángel, 22, has moved to Craven Cottage. Fulham describe their new signings as “a two-footed central midfield player, comfortable with the ball at his feet, is intelligent with his movement, and has a keen eye for a pass.” All that for an undisclosed fee.

Lamine Camara a eu sa photo avec Frank Lampard ! 😄❤️ pic.twitter.com/gjaZQCRIEH

A bit more on Ait-Nouri. He was offered to United by a third party a few days ago and they then enquired to City this afternoon to see if a loan was feasible. But a loan would only have been possible with an obligation to buy yet United were not interested in committing themselves to a permanent deal for the player.

Nottingham Forest have established an unwanted reputation for hectic business on deadline day but today is very likely to be a sign that things are changing.

Forest are not expected to make any signings before the deadline and are perfectly happy with their squad.

The big signings have been Liam Delap (£45m from Chelsea), Ousmane Diomande (£34m from Sporting CP) and Daniel Munoz (£20m from Crystal Palace).

Forest did want to sign a central midfielder, with bids for Tottenham’s Lucas Bergvall and Everton’s Harrison Armstrong rejected, but the general feeling is one of calm.

Arnaud Kalimuendo is also going to stay at the City Ground despite strong interest from Eintracht Frankfurt in re-signing him after he impressed on loan over the second half of last season.

Chelsea have agreed a £47m fee with Monaco to sign midfielder Lamine Camara. It’s late in the day, but all sides are optimistic this one will get done.

Manchester United made a deadline day enquiry to rivals Manchester City about Rayan Ait-Nouri but were told the Algeria left-back was not available.

Meanwhile, Everton have made a late move for forward Joshua Zirkzee.

Chelsea’s transfer window might not be over. Sources in France believe the club may still sign Lamine Camara from Monaco before the window shuts. Chelsea had a £38m bid for Camara turned down earlier today but the door has reopened after Folarin Balogun’s proposed move to Everton stalled. Stand by your beds...

Iliman Ndiaye has been confirmed as a Manchester City signing. He moves on a five-year deal from Everton with the deal worth £65m.

The fee means Premier League spending has now surpassed the previous record for a summer window which stood at £3.14bn. The running tally now stands at £3.193bn.

Ndiaye says: “I’ve worked my whole life for an opportunity like this. City are one of the best clubs in the world and I’ve seen them win everything as I’ve grown up.

“To be able to write my own chapter in a story that special is the chance of a lifetime and I’m determined to grab it with both hands.

“It’s not always been easy in my career, but I always had the belief that I could play for a team challenging for the biggest prizes and now I’m here. It feels so good.

“I love to play with the ball on the floor in an attacking team that wants to score as many goals as possible. That’s why I know this is the perfect fit.

“City fans can rest assured that I will give my all to bring more success to this incredible club.”

Welcome to City, Iliman 🩵 pic.twitter.com/u3WWUpVQOg

Harry Amass looks like he’s staying at Old Trafford and Louis Page’s proposed move to United from Leicester is off after a failure to reach an agreement. Willem II are trying to sign Chido Obi on loan. As reported earlier, not expecting United to sign a left-back, barring a dramatic turn of events, so not the deadline day or end to the window United fans will have hoped for.

Significant – and dispiriting – news for Everton. Folarin Balogun has failed a medical and it appears that his £40m move from Monaco is off. The club are yet to confirm any news but the indications are this is a devastating blow for both the player and the club.

Wilfried Gnonto has joined Fiorentina on a season-long loan with a £15m buy option. That could open the door for Jean-Matteo Bahoya to sign from Eintracht Frankfurt.

Wilfried Gnonto entra a far parte della nostra Storia💜⚜️ pic.twitter.com/xhqTryvZDE

That is the moniker given to Stuttgart’s 21-year-old Spanish midfielder Chema Andrés, who came through the system at Real Madrid. Real will receive half of the £18.8m fee thanks to a sell-on clause. What price he joins Chelsea next summer for fourfold what Brighton are paying?

Usurped as Chelsea’s first-choice goalkeeper, Sanchez is on his way to Italy where he will play under Cesc Fabregas. Como also completed the signing of former Juventus and Everton striker Moise Kean today.

Fabregas said: “Robert brings experience at the highest level and qualities that suit the way we want to play. He is a strong goalkeeper with a big presence, but he is also very comfortable with the ball and can help us build from the back.”

He joins from Spurs on a season-long loan and the deal features a buy option. Sunderland’s statement reads: “A commanding centre-back, Danso has won hearts throughout his career, with his committed performances.” Who knew the Austria centre-half was the object of so much affection?

Follow his lead... pic.twitter.com/Pb1s8nfKED

Nottingham Forest defender Morato has completed his move to West Ham United.

Morato has joined the Championship club on an initial loan with West Ham holding an option to make the move permanent.

West Ham’s manager Nuno Espirito Santo signed the Brazilian centre-back during his spell with Forest.

Crystal Palace are having a frantic end to the transfer window, with Ben Chilwell also a deal they are pursuing.

The former England left-back, 29, is at Strasbourg where he is in the final year of his contract. Palace are also trying for Quinten Timber from Marseille and are still in the race for Lyon’s Malick Fofana.

Ethan Nwaneri has completed his loan move from Arsenal to Borussia Dortmund. A lot of Arsenal fans will be pleased he hasn’t been sold, which was a real possibility this summer. Hopefully this move is more successful than his time in Marseille in the second half of last season, when the chaos at the club did not help the teenager to settle.

Liverpool’s last significant business for the window is done with the completion of the £30m deal for goalkeeper Lucca Brughmans from Genk. The 18-year-old will remain in Belgium, to play the season with his current club.

He has been bought with the future in mind and Liverpool are covering all bases, as Alisson Becker – who has been the undisputed No 1 since he arrived in 2018 – is now in the final year of his contract. Liverpool also spent £33m on Giorgi Mamardashvili last summer.

Alisson could have left this summer, with Juventus initially keen to sign him. Either way, this points to Liverpool making plans for a new generation.

Never quite lived up to his billing as a Berbatov-Havertz hybrid, scoring 11 goals in 53 appearances for Newcastle in all competitions last season when the idea of him leading the line was slowly abandoned. Serie A should suit him better, and Newcastle have confirmed his move to Italy.

His £60m move from Arsenal to Al-Hilal is yet to be finalised or confirmed, but it appears well on the way to completion. Tonight’s 11pm deadline does not apply to the Saudi window, which will stay open for another six weeks.

Crystal Palace midfielder Justin Devenny is undergoing a medical at Championship club Stoke City.

Devenny, 22, is a Northern Ireland international and is close to joining Stoke on a permanent basis.

Palace midfielder David Ozoh could also leave before the deadline, with Derby County keen to re-sign their former loan signing again.

Speaking about the Enzo Fernández deal on Sky Sports, Carragher said: “It pushes them above Chelsea. Myself and plenty of others felt Chelsea would have a really good season, and I still believe that.

“A lot of that is on the back of no European football, having a new manager and the front three they have got.

“But losing Enzo Fernandez, who for me over the last two or three years has been one of the big players for Chelsea... they’ve always had five or six top players but maybe not a lot around them.

“They’ve let one of them go, to Man City, it’s a huge fee but City look a lot stronger now and I’d say they are going to be the main challengers to Arsenal.”

Crystal Palace are making a late move for Quinten Timber in a deal from Marseille. The 25-year-old Netherlands international has been on Palace’s radar for a central midfield role. He is the twin brother of Arsenal defender Jurrien.

Happy birthday to the Timber twins: Quinten and Jurrien! 🇳🇱❤️ pic.twitter.com/dktRvPQwOQ

According to Sky Germany, Brighton are keen on 21-year-old Chema Andrés from Stuttgart. He started 14 games in the Bundesliga last season, and came through the ranks at Real Madrid.

Leeds are lining up Eintracht Frankfurt forward Jean-Matteo Bahoya as Willy Gnonto is waiting on move to Fiorentina.

Chelsea had been holding off from sanctioning Enzo Fernández’s move to Manchester City while they searched for a new midfielder of their own.

But City’s willingness to agree a £125m package has convinced Chelsea to give the green light to the Fernández move without any guarantees over an incoming signing.

Chelsea still have a few hours to try to make something happen, having had a bid for Lamine Camara turned down.

But Chelsea ultimately felt they had no choice but to let Fernández, who made it clear he wanted to leave, go in the best interests of the club.

Chelsea believe they have a strong squad, regardless of whether or not a new player is signed today, and will continue to weigh up their options.

The medicals are under way for Jack Grealish, Ainsley Maitland-Niles and Folarin Balogun at Everton but there is no clarity on when all three deals will be concluded. It must be stressed that no issues are envisaged and they will be the only additions to the squad before the window closes. No further departures are expected, either.

On the other side of the city, things are winding down for Liverpool. Harvey Elliott’s loan to Valencia will be officially announced in due course. It is a straight loan, without an obligation to buy.

Fulham are progressing quite quickly on three deals: Hugo Larsson (Frankfurt), Manuel Angel (Real Madrid) and David Affengruber (Elche).

Sunderland now believe their move for Malick Fofana is back on despite Crystal Palace’s attempt to hijack the deal...

Chelsea have agreed a £125m package to sell Enzo Fernández to Manchester City so the saga is finally coming to a close.

Chelsea will be happy with a fee that equals the British transfer record and City head coach Enzo Maresca will be delighted to land his top target.

It feels like a win-win all round as Fernández wanted to leave Chelsea and the club wanted over £120m after their initial deadline to do a deal expired.

It remains to be seen if Chelsea land any of their three main deadline day targets with a few hours of the window to go.

Chelsea had a bid rejected for Lamine Camara, Roma have not been playing ball on Manu Kone and the identity of the mystery Premier League target has not yet emerged.

Newcastle insist the only deals they are working on for the rest of the day are the departures of Nick Woltemade on loan to Juventus and Sean Neave to Wolverhampton Wanderers.

Multiple sources deny there is any chance of Jacob Murphy leaving for Nottingham Forest despite claims of a second bid being rejected today.

High drama on Wearside where Sunderland fear their deal to sign Malick Fofana from Lyon has been hijacked by Crystal Palace.

Nobody has told Sunderland the deal is off yet, but the fact they are also lining up an alternative in the shape of Dodi Lukébakio shows they are worried.

It is understood Sunderland have made contact with Benfica this afternoon to discuss terms for Lukébakio, who is another Belgium international.

Crystal Palace are believed to have offered more money to Lyon and higher wages to Fofana which could be enough to swing things in their favour.

Manchester United are in discussions about signing the 18-year-old Leicester midfielder Louis Page. Talks ongoing with Leicester but there are no guarantees a deal will happen at this stage.

As things stand, Joshua Zirkzee seems more likely to stay at United than go. The prospects of bringing in a left-back are also fading.

Who you gon' call? ☎️ pic.twitter.com/SS0xYHtONL

West Ham are in a state of flux, trying to find their way in the Championship, and they have failed with a bid to take Michael Keane from Everton on loan. They had offers from Werder Bremen and Sevilla, too, to take Edson Álvarez out on a season-long loan. The interest from Sevilla in the Mexican was strong and the proposal would have covered all of Álvarez’s wages but West Ham were looking to recoup a significant loan fee to sanction it. That detail led to the deal falling through.

When Newcastle United’s recruitment team finalised their list of priority targets back in the spring Matías Fernández-Pardo featured prominently.

There was excitement about what he could bring to the team. There was a buzz of possibility. The 21-year-old forward had impressed everyone, from scouts to decision makers. The call to make him one of their first-choice targets, alongside Switzerland international Johan Manzambi, was unanimous. Just as it had been when Newcastle identified Alexander Isak as their leading target back in the summer of 2022.

These meetings are a place for ideas to be shared and different targets pushed. Everyone had their own opinion and various favourites, but Fernández-Pardo was, in the words of one member of Newcastle’s recruitment taskforce “the one”.

Moussa Diaby, the former Aston Villa winger, has put pen to paper on a second spell at Bayer Leverkusen, where he scored 49 goals in four seasons. He arrives in Germany after a two-year stint at Al-Ittihad in the Saudi Pro League.

Japanese centre-back Kota Takai has completed a loan move to Belgian Pro League side Sint-Truidense VV. He follows Souza and Mikey Moore, who Spurs have also loaned out to Porto and Cologne respectively.

In England, the transfer window slams shut at 11pm, but the deadline to complete deals is earlier on the Continent:

In the Scottish Premiership, deals can be completed until 5pm on Thursday, September 3.

Former Wolves, Fulham and West Ham winger Adama Traore has joined La Liga side Deportivo A Coruna.

💙🆕 @AdamaTrd37 x @RCDeportivo. #LALIGATransfers | #LALIGAEASPORTS pic.twitter.com/JskGd6alNK

Once one of the fastest players in the world, Traore will join forces with another speedy forward in Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang to complete a vintage Premier League frontline...

Although much of the chatter today has related to Enzo Fernandez, a name that has cropped up a lot over the past hours has been that of Malick Fofana.

Sunderland had seemingly beaten Arsenal to the Lyon winger’s signature but reports have emerged that Crystal Palace are attempting to hijack Fofana’s Wearside move...

We’re still awaiting official confirmation of Mykhailo Mudryk’s loan move to Tottenham Hotspur. It would mean a reunion with Roberto De Zerbi, under whom the Ukrainian played at Shakhtar Donetsk.

When asked about Mudryk in 2022, the then Brighton head coach said: “Mykhailo has the potential for a top career. In my opinion, he can also win the Ballon d’Or. He is a player of the highest level but he is also very sensitive.”

De Zerbi added: “He needs affection. We will see if he matches his potential.”

Gabriel Jesus has completed his move from Arsenal to Barcelona in a deal worth about £9m. It’s a fantastic move for the Brazilian, who had declined in importance at Arsenal after a succession of serious injuries. Arsenal would have hoped for a higher fee for a player of his reputation but his enormous salary, believed to have been worth about £250,000 a week, was always going to be problematic as they looked for buyers.

When instinct calls, you answer. ☎️ pic.twitter.com/BgZktIcJ17

The 18-year-old centre-back will become a Chelsea player in the summer of 2027, but will spend the rest of this season on loan at Selhurst Park from Atalanta.

A brief update on Jayden Danns: he is going to stay at Liverpool, rather than accept a loan in Europe. There is some significance to this as, if you had read Telegraph Sport 10 days ago, you will know that Liverpool are in a position where for the first time in 134 years, a player born within the city might not represent them. Danns is the one who can keep the record going.

How is your team’s squad shaping up heading into the last stages of the window?

Sam Johnstone is heading to Celtic ahead of a loan deal from Wolves.

The 33-year-old, capped four times by England under Gareth Southgate, is travelling to Scotland this afternoon to completed the formalities of the deal including a medical.

Ainsley Maitland-Niles has emerged as a prime target for Everton, as they look to find a solution to their right-back conundrum. The former Arsenal defender, who is now at Lyon, has been the subject of a £5m offer and the indication is that he has now taken over from Kenny Tete as the preferred option. Everton, historically, have always pushed things to the wire on transfer deadline day and this one is proving to be no different.

With Woltemade travelling to undergo a medical with Juventus for a loan move from Newcastle, that would appear to shut off one potential exit route for Joshua Zirkzee. Juventus had been looking at a season long loan for Zirkzee. Fiorentina have also been keen on Zirkzee and made an offer to United of a loan plus €30m (£25.7m) buy option but the Netherlands forward turned down the chance to go there. United would be more likely to bring in another player, probably a left-back rather than a direct replacement, if Zirkzee was to go but time running out on that front.

United had hoped to sell Manuel Ugarte and Zirkzee this summer and were in the market for buyers for Marcus Rashford, but the window could close with all three staying put. Ugarte’s serious knee injury put paid to the Uruguay midfielder leaving and Rashford has been reintergrated in the squad after Barcelona opted against taking up an option to sign him permanently.

Benfica are in talks about loaning Argentina Under-23 forward Claudio Echeverri from Manchester City, It’s likely to be a season long loan with an option to buy if finalised.

Fabio Vieira has completed his move from Arsenal to Hamburg, in a deal believed to be worth about £9m. The Portuguese midfielder has never cut it in the Premier League and it is no surprise that Arsenal have cashed in. They paid more than £30m to sign him from Porto in 2022 but he has never come close to justifying the fee. In truth, it’s one of their worst transfers under Mikel Arteta.

Southampton forward Cameron Archer is on course to sign for Auxerre on a season-long loan.

Archer has been a target for a number of Championship clubs this summer but a deal has been problematic because of his £35,000-a-week wages.

It is understood Southampton have been demanding that his salary be paid in full, which has scared off interested clubs in the second tier.

Chelsea will hold off sanctioning Enzo Fernández’s move to Manchester City until they are confident of making at least one signing of their own.

Telegraph Sport understands that Chelsea have already rejected one proposal from City for Fernández during club-to-club talks and are demanding a fee and payment terms that are favourable to them.

Chelsea also have three separate targets of their own as potential deadline signings – Lamine Camara, Manu Kone and one mystery target from the Premier League.

Monaco have already rejected a £38.5m bid from Chelsea for Camara. Roma manager Gian Piero Gasperini wants to keep Kone, although negotiations continue. And there is a third target from the Premier League, who is not believed to be Morgan Gibbs-White.

Chelsea must make significant progress on one of their targets before they will sanction Fernández’s sale – and City must make another bid that is more favourable to the club.

Monaco have rejected an opening €45m bid from Chelsea for midfielder Lamine Camara. It now remains to be seen if the club increase that offer.

Sunderland have been trying to sign a winger all summer and it appears that they have finally got their man in Lyon’s Malick Fofana.

Arsenal had been linked with a move for the 21-year old Belgium international.

Plenty of chatter about the future of Roma midfielder Manu Koné, who is linked with a move to Chelsea. The France international would be a strong acquisition for Xabi Alonso, but could his potential signing precede an Enzo Fernández exit? All will be revealed in due course...

Of Koné, former France manager Didier Deschamps said: “He’s very effective at winning the ball back, but he shouldn’t be limited to that role of defensive midfielder, because he also makes a difference in his use of the ball.”

Austria centre-back David Affengruber has emerged as potential deadline-day deal for Fulham as they look to bolster Alvaro Arbeloa’s defence.

The Elche player has been in La Liga for two years playing regularly and fits the data model at Craven Cottage.

Fulham are also trying deals for Real Madrid’s Manuel Angel and Eintracht Frankfurt’s Hugo Larsson as midfield options.

Sunderland are expected to complete the signing of centre-back Kevin Danso from Tottenham Hotspur with the player travelling to Wearside last night for the first part of his medical.

The Austria international will initially join on loan with an obligation to make the move permanent for £25m next year.

Danso had made it clear he wanted to leave Tottenham this summer in search of regular first-team football.

Eintracht Frankfurt are in talks with Nottingham Forest over another loan move for forward Arnaud Kalimuendo.

Frankfurt signed the Frenchman on loan in January and are negotiating a return for Forest’s £26m signing from Rennes.

Oliver Glasner, Forest’s head coach, had been intent on keeping Kalimuendo but it is understood Frankfurt’s strong interest has altered the club’s thinking.

Morato, the centre-back, is expected to join West Ham United on loan.

Forest are exploring potential signings but are determined to stay calm and only pursue deals that make financial sense. A winger and a No 6 are the two priority targets if there are deals to be done.

On Tuesday evening, the Tottenham and Brazil forward posted an emotional message on Instagram amid reports of a possible move back to Everton.

He wrote: “After everything I’ve been through in recent years, I decided that never again would others decide my future for me.

“I went through a lot of bad things during this time, and almost all of them happened because of decisions made by other people. Pressure, threats, retaliation – none of that scares me. I’ve been through worse, believe me!

“I have always made it clear at every opportunity that my departure to another place would also have to be good for the club. If it wasn’t, I would never accept it... just as I didn’t accept it when everything here was falling apart and they needed me.”

Richarlison added: “I stayed and gave my all. So, I hope they treat my situation with the same respect that I have always had for Spurs and for all the people who worked with me during this period. Just don’t try to decide for me.”

“If Spurs and Everton reach an agreement, I will return to the club of my heart. My intention was indeed to go back to the place where I was very happy.

“But negotiations were being done the way other people wanted, and it won’t be that way anymore. Despite all this turmoil, I have a contract with Spurs and I will remain at the club’s disposal.”

It will be good news for Arsenal if Folarin Balogun completes his £40m move to Everton today. When Arsenal sold Balogun to Monaco in 2023, they negotiated a sell-on clause of 17.5 per cent. According to my maths, that means Arsenal will get £7m from this transfer. Not to be sniffed at!

Hull City are close to agreeing a fee of around £7.5m for Stoke City winger Sorba Thomas.

The Wales international has been a long-term target for Hull and negotiations are now approaching a conclusion.

Thomas has been pushing a move through and is expected to leave Stoke after one full season.

As has become the norm this summer Acun Ilicali has posted a cryptic message on X, which has prompted speculation among Hull City fans. The club has been linked with Everton holding midfielder Tim Iroegbunam.

The La Masia graduate secures a permanent move to Germany. Who knows how his career in England would have panned out had Chelsea not recalled him 25 days into his Sunderland loan at the beginning of last season...

Marc Guiu has completed a permanent transfer to Bundesliga side RB Leipzig. Everyone at Chelsea would like to thank Marc for his efforts during his time at the club and wish him every success as he begins the next chapter of his career with RB Leipzig.

What a couple of weeks it has been for Robert Sanchez. He came into this season as Chelsea’s No 1, but after a difficult start to the campaign and Emi Martinez’s arrival, reports suggest he could be moving away from Stamford Bridge on loan. Cesc Fabregas’s Como appears the probable destination.

Trevoh Chalobah, who left Chelsea for Como last month, has taken to his “secondary” Instagram account to post the following picture...

Meanwhile, as reported by Telegraph Sport yesterday, striker flop Nick Woltemade is moving to Juventus on a season-long loan. The club’s record signing from as year ago at £64m is moving to Turin for a £3.5m loan fee with the Serie A squad covering the full cost of his wages.

Newcastle will complete the £51m signing of forward Matias Fernandez-Pardo from Lille today but that is expected to be it in terms of incomings.

The Belgium international will become the club’s eighth signing of the summer and his versatility – he can play as a centre forward, a No 10 or out wide – means there are no more gaps to fill in the squad.

In an ideal world, Newcastle would have liked to sign another defender but none of their targets were still on the market. With Dan Burn due to return from injury in a few weeks, they have four centre-backs while new arrival Amar Dedic can play on both sides as a full-back.

In terms of outgoings, Joe Willock and Jacob Murphy are expected to stay at the club despite interest from Nottingham Forest and Besiktas. Young striker Sean Neave will be allowed to leave on loan. The 19-year-old has offers from clubs in the Championship and League One but Newcastle want him to go somewhere he has the best chance of getting regular first-team football.

City have been this summer’s selling kings and have had six players leave the club in deals worth more than £45m. Compare that to the summer when Pep Guardiola first arrived at the club, in 2016, when City generated just £23m from sales and made losses on Edin Dzeko and Stevan Jovetic, while Martín Demichelis departed on a free transfer.

Fast forward to this summer and more than £300m worth of players have been sold, with a further £60m arriving at the end of the season when Omar Marmoush’s loan to Tottenham Hotspur becomes permanent.

Given how Jaissle wants Newcastle to play, it is plain to see why Fernandez-Pardo appeals to him. Quick, direct and only 21 – he would surely fit right in at St James’ Park.

The Leeds wide man has a medical booked with Fiorentina today. He made a handful of appearances for Daniel Farke’s side during pre-season but has not featured since the start of the 2026-27 campaign.

✈️ L'arrivo di Gnonto a Firenze ⚜️ pic.twitter.com/nEFngsyxQP

Very unlikely that Liverpool will be doing any major incoming business but there may yet be some departures. Jayden Danns, who broke through three years ago and played in the 2024 League Cup final defeat of Chelsea, is attracting interest from clubs in Europe, who want to take him on loan. Danns, a promising striker, has had injury issues and is working his way back to full fitness but his long-term ambition is to prove to Andoni Iraola that he can be part of his squad.

Fax machines are whirring as the clock continues to tick towards the transfer deadline, but who does your club need to sign? Let us know in the comments below!

Aston Villa are to confirm the signings of £50m winger Ibrahim Mbaye and £25m centre-back Taylor Harwood-Bellis this morning.

Mbaye and Harwood-Bellis takes the number of Villa’s signings this summer to 10, with Unai Emery ruling out any more additions after the 1-0 defeat by Arsenal last night.

Emery also disclosed that forward Tammy Abraham will be staying at Villa Park, amid interest from Ipswich Town.

The one player who could leave today is Jamaica international Leon Bailey, who has interest from clubs in Europe, and Hull City.

Nottingham Forest can confirm Omari Hutchinson has joined AC Milan on a season-long loan deal, with the Italian club holding an option to make the transfer permanent.Everyone at Nottingham Forest wishes Omari all the best for his time in Italy. pic.twitter.com/fSv1uNGh2Y

Fulham remain locked in discussions with Rayo Vallecano to agree a fee for right-back Andrei Ratiu, with the Romania international having confirmed he wants to join Alvaro Arbeloa’s side. The spin-off with this deal is that it will accelerate Kenny Tete’s switch to Everton, for a fee in the region of £9.5m.

On the subject of right-backs, Nathan Patterson, who has had a difficult time at Everton, has been granted permission to travel to Italy to undergo a medical with Torino.

Matias Fernandez-Pardo is on the verge of joining Newcastle United, and Luke Edwards reported that the forward’s arrival is likely to pave the way for Nick Woltemade’s departure.

The German enjoyed a fruitful start to life in England after signing last summer, scoring seven Premier League goals before the turn of the year, but could only manage one goal in the second half of the season. While Eddie Howe experimented with Woltemade in a more withdrawn No 10 role, there was a clear drop-off in his game-time after Christmas.

Newcastle are ready to pay around £51m to sign Fernandez-Pardo after holding face-to-face talks with Lille last week. The 21-year-old is a versatile attacker and Newcastle identified him as a top target months ago. If they can complete a deal, it could speed up the departure of Nick Woltemade, who is wanted by Juventus.

The Brazilian has asked to leave Spurs and has been linked to a move back to Everton. However, his hopes of returning to Merseyside may have taken a hit on Monday night, when Everton agreed a £40m deal with Monaco for striker Folarin Balogun.

Brighton are keen to sign Azeez from Millwall and have made multiple offers for the forward. Millwall want at least £15m for Azeez, who scored 11 goals in the Championship last season. Ipswich Town have previously shown interest in Azeez.

Leeds are signing Melvin Bard on loan from Nice. One-season deal for the 25-year-old who will compete for a place in the first-team under Daniel Farke.

We’re expecting four departures from Arsenal today. Nwaneri to Dortmund on loan (see my colleague Mike McGrath’s post below), Gabriel Martinelli to Al-Hilal, Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona and Fabio Vieira to Hamburg. Those deals should raise around £70m.

Will there be any incomings? The Julian Alvarez situation seems unlikely to develop in Arsenal’s favour, barring a dramatic change of heart. As reported by Telegraph Sport yesterday, Lyon winger Malick Fofana is a potential option.

Borussia Dortmund have been trying to close out a loan deal for Arsenal winger Ethan Nwaneri, as reported by Telegraph Sport yesterday. The German club have previously attempted to land the 19-year-old and this time want him on a deal for the season.

It is expected to be another busy deadline day in the Premier League, with many clubs still hoping to finalise deals before the transfer window shuts at 11pm. Here, Telegraph Sport identifies 10 potential high-profile moves that could yet go through.

This has been the most dramatic and relentless saga of the European transfer window. The situation, as far as we understand it, is as follows: Barcelona want Alvarez and Alvarez wants Barcelona, but Atletico Madrid refuse to sell him to Barcelona. Arsenal want Alvarez, and Atletico are more open to selling him to Arsenal, but Alvarez only wants Barcelona. For a move to happen, it will require one party to change their mind. Either Atletico decides to sell to Barcelona, or Alvarez decides he will join Arsenal.

Another long-running saga. Chelsea are well aware of City’s interest in Fernandez but want a massive fee for the Argentina international, having initially valued him at £120m. City have the cash and the space in the squad after saying goodbye to Rodri, Tijani Reijnders, Nico Gonzalez and Bernardo Silva this summer. Fernandez has not featured in Chelsea’s last two games.

As reported by Telegraph Sport last week, Chelsea have identified Monaco midfielder Camara as a target amid the uncertainty over Fernandez’s future. French reports on Monday suggested the move may have stalled, however. The clock is ticking.

Spurs had been working on a deal to sign Ndiaye from Everton but they now appear to have fallen behind City in the race for the winger, as a consequence of City failing in their attempt to sign Cody Gakpo from Liverpool. City are ready to complete the hijack on deadline day.

A deal that, as of Monday night, is regarded as unlikely to happen. As with their interest in Brighton’s Yankuba Minteh, Liverpool have so far been unable to strike a deal with Crystal Palace for Sarr, who scored 21 goals in 45 games last season. Liverpool would only allow Gakpo to leave if a replacement, such as Sarr, can be signed.

Burnley are one of a host of Championship clubs who are interested in the young Manchester United left-back Harry Amass. There have been talks over a potential permanent deal but a loan cannot be ruled out. The 19-year-old joined United from Watford in 2023.

Everton have reached an agreement with Manchester City to sign Jack Grealish on another season long loan. It has been a very busy summer of outgoings at City and Grealish will be the latest to depart as he prepares to return to Merseyside. He started well at Everton last season before injury in January derailed his campaign.

A big year ahead for the English midfielder.

Tottenham are set to complete a double deal for Chelsea pair Mykhailo Mudryk and Tosin Adarabioyo after missing out on Iliman Ndiaye.

Spurs will take Mudryk on loan for the season having seen their attempt to land Ndiaye fail when Manchester City agreed a £65m deal with Everton.

Mudryk, 25, worked with Spurs head coach Roberto De Zerbi at Shakthtar Donetsk, in the winger’s homeland Ukraine, before his £85m move to Chelsea in 2023.

Leeds United had shown interest but instead he will be reunited with De Zerbi, effectively taking Ndiaye’s place as a wide-forward option.

Adarabioyo will be a permanent deal to Spurs as they are not allowed to loan two players from a Premier League club.

Good morning and welcome to live coverage of transfer deadline day. We are deep into stoppage time in this summer window and we will bring you the key developments as teams scramble to get last-minute deals over the line before the full-time whistle blows at 11pm.

Enzo Fernández remains a City target, and his omission from Xabi Alonso’s match-day squad against Brighton and Hove Albion on Sunday has only added weight to the feeling that he might reunite with former Chelsea head coach Enzo Maresca. City would be required to meet the Londoners’ £120m asking price, which is just shy of Alexander Isak’s £125m British record fee.

Meanwhile, Julián Alvarez’s situation at Atlético Madrid continues to be monitored by Arsenal. The Argentina forward’s dream move to Barcelona appears a no-goer as Atlético remain steadfast in their refusal to sell to their La Liga rivals. While this could bring Arsenal into the picture, it is understood that Alvarez – who missed three training sessions last week and did not travel to Sevilla with Diego Simeone’s squad on Saturday – is not pursuing a return to England.

A Mohamed Salah-shaped hole on Liverpool’s right flank has been filled by Bradley Barcola after the club agreed a £123m deal with Paris St-Germain. His signing looked as though it might trigger Cody Gakpo’s move away from Anfield as the winger had been linked with a move to Manchester City, but it appears that the Netherlands international will stay put. Maresca’s side have instead hijacked Spurs’ move for Iliman Ndiaye, and the north London outfit pivoted to take Myhailo Mudryk and Tosin Adarabioyo from Chelsea, on loan and permanent deals respectively. Liverpool could yet swoop for Brighton’s Yankuba Minteh or Ismaïla Sarr.

Newcastle United appeared to have reached their nadir this summer after Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimarães and Eddie Howe departed, but Matthias Jaissle has breathed life into St James’ Park by delivering an exciting brand of football that leans on the team’s explosive pace in forward positions. Lille’s Matias Fernandez-Pardo would fit this system and is on the brink of joining Newcastle in a deal worth £51m, which could signal Nick Woltemade’s exit.

Barcola is the window’s most expensive acquisition, followed by Morgan Rogers who was prised away from Aston Villa to the tune of £118m, and has already hit the ground running for the Londoners. He cost £2m more than his England team-mate Elliot Anderson, who swapped Nottingham Forest for Manchester City. Elite midfielders have proved a gilded commodity with seven of the Premier League’s top 10 most expensive acquisitions coming in the middle of the park. The departures of Rodri, Casemiro and others will have played their part.

Praying for a deadline-day saviour or counting down the seconds until the window slams shut on directors of football hoping to lure away your club’s next big thing? Let us know in the comments and join the conversation as the day unfolds.

#1744. Everton team news: Jack Grealish omission explained before Newcastle Premier League clash

By Oliver Thomas | 02 Nov 2026 15:31, Last updated: 02 Nov 2026 15:33

Jack Grealish is expected to be left out of Everton’s squad for tonight’s Premier League clash away against Newcastle United, according to a report.

The 31-year-old was omitted from the senior squad for the Toffees’ EFL Cup home win over the Magpies on Thursday due to a ‘breach of club discipline’.

Although manager David Moyes did not confirmed the exact reason behind Grealish’s absence, it is understood that the winger failed to show up for a training session in the build-up to the fourth-round tie.

The Manchester City loanee had previously missed Everton’s 2-0 Premier League defeat at Arsenal just over a week ago due to illness.

According to The Athletic, Grealish is 'not fit' to face Newcastle and has subsequently not travelled with the rest of Everton’s squad for this evening’s game at St James’ Park.

The report adds that it is unclear whether Grealish will return for Everton’s next fixture at home to Coventry City on Friday.

Speaking after Everton’s EFL Cup win, Moyes revealed that he supported the club’s decision to drop Grealish, but refused to comment further on the matter.

Grealish is in his second season on loan at Everton from Man City; a long-term injury cut his first spell short, but his standout early performances made him a massive hit with the fans.

However, the winger has struggled to make his mark this term, failing to score or assist in any of his eight appearances across all competitions.

The lack of depth in the Everton squad is a persistent issue for Moyes, and having to cope without Grealish only exacerbates the problem, leaving the Toffees light in the attacking department.

Tyrique George and Brennan Johnson appear to be the most likely duo to operate on the flanks in Grealish’s absence, though Tyler Dibling is another winger pushing for start.

Dibling and George both started on Thursday against Newcastle, with Johnson coming on as a 75th-minute substitute for the former.

Everton currently sit 14th in the Premier League table, one point and two places behind Newcastle in 12th spot.

The Anfield side spent around £450m that summer - on players like Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz, Hugo Ekitike and others - but got worse.

LFC unravel under Richard HughesArne Slot paid with his job with Hughes overseeing the appointment of Andoni Iraola as a replacement. #1739. Opinion: Sensational, The Premier League's most important star is officially Liverpool's

Liverpool boast the Premier League's most important player right now. What an incredible season he's having so far.

Things felt like an absolute mess at Liverpool heading into the summer and they didn't exactly feel tidy coming out of it. That's not because the Reds didn't have good players, nor were they even in a Manchester United kind of mess.

The problem was that Liverpool had a title winning team in 2025 and then proceeded to spend an awful lot of money tearing it up. Record-breaking amounts went out on players but none delivered. If we're honest, we're still waiting to see a return for the cash.

Of course, when you've got players this good, you can only do so badly. A 'poor' season for Liverpool is still one where they qualify for European football - but the money spent means the standards are sky high.

You want to see these players delivering at the absolute elite level, something that simply didn't happen over the 2025/26 campaign. But we might finally be seeing it.

The Alexander Isak showLiverpool made Isak the most expensive player in English football history in 2025 when they bought him from Newcastle United. His first season, however, was a disaster. Isak had essentially skipped pre-season in an effort to force the transfer, meaning he arrived at Liverpool half-fit. That's probably an exaggeration, actually - he was barely fit at all. By the time he finally got going, he broke his leg. It meant that Liverpool's record signing provided a grand total of three Premier League goals in his debut season. A figure he has already doubled in this campaign with his six coming in just seven fixtures.

Liverpool made Isak the most expensive player in English football history in 2025 when they bought him from Newcastle United. His first season, however, was a disaster.

Isak had essentially skipped pre-season in an effort to force the transfer, meaning he arrived at Liverpool half-fit. That's probably an exaggeration, actually - he was barely fit at all. By the time he finally got going, he broke his leg.

It meant that Liverpool's record signing provided a grand total of three Premier League goals in his debut season. A figure he has already doubled in this campaign with his six coming in just seven fixtures.

But more importantly, it's when Isak has scored the goals that really catches the eye. They've come in five different matches and have directly delivered seven points across the campaign. Only two other players can match that: Erling Haaland and Nicolas Jackson.

Strip those points away and Liverpool drop all the way down to 16th on eight points. That's so low that they're only barely still ahead of Manchester United (17th in the Premier League table on seven points after nine (9) matches).

This is ultimately why Liverpool paid the money. Isak is proving himself to be incredibly decisive, bagging his goals across multiple games and in important ways, rather than hat tricks in 6-0 drubbings.

Finally, Liverpool's 2025 rebuild might be clicking together and reaching the standards it called for.

#1736. Lens vs Como - prediction, team news, lineups

By Jonathan O'Shea | 02 Nov 2026 15:38, Last updated: 02 Nov 2026 15:40

Languishing outside the Champions League's top 24, Lens will aim to move level with Como when they meet at Stade Bollaert-Delelis on Wednesday night.

Following their historic defeat of Manchester United, the Italian debutants have put six points on the board, while their hosts only have three and lie below the playoff zone.

Since Lens started their fourth Champions League campaign with a thrilling 3-2 comeback win over Slavia Prague, the French club have come away empty-handed from their subsequent fixtures.

Les Sang et Or were first beaten 2-0 at home by Sporting Lisbon, then suffered another defeat on their travels, going down 3-0 to Club Brugge.

Remarkably, 16 games and some 28 years have now passed since they last kept a clean sheet in the Champions League.

Lens returned to Europe's top table by finishing second in Ligue 1 last term but, after a slow start, new boss Dino Toppmoller swiftly made way for Yannick Cahuzac.

Though Toppmoller's former assistant started positively with three straight league wins, his side were beaten by their bitter local rivals last time out.

With a late Olivier Giroud goal, Lille snatched victory in the 125th Derby du Nord on Friday night, leaving Lens ninth in the French top flight.

Now, Cahuzac's side must try to respond with maximum points, as they surely need at least two more wins from five remaining Champions League matches.

Como took one step closer to the knockout phase last month, thumping Manchester United 4-1 on a memorable night at Stadio Sinigaglia, where main man Nico Paz bagged a brace.

Regardless of United's dire state, that marked an incredible achievement for a club promoted back to Italy's top tier only two years earlier - and they were down in Serie D as recently as 2019.

Expertly led by Cesc Fabregas, 10 goals from their first three games is the best haul of any debutant in UEFA's elite competition since 1973 - and each one has been scored from open play.

Paz and top scorer Tasos Douvikas already have five Champions League strikes between them, and the pair have been even more productive in Serie A, with 11 goal involvements combined.

Since losing 3-2 to Feyenoord on matchday two, Como have embarked on a streak of five consecutive wins across all competitions, scoring 13 goals and conceding just three.

New France cap Lucas Da Cunha was decisive from the spot in Sunday's 1-0 victory against rock-bottom Venezia, taking the Lariani up to a club-record tally of 23 points from their opening 10 games.

Now occupying fourth place - where they finished last term - Como are closely in touch with Italy's current top three, and few would rule them out of the Scudetto race.

Lens will be missing several men on Wednesday, with defensive duo Ismaelo Ganiou and Maik Nawrocki joining forwards Abdalllah Sima and Odsonne Edouard on the sidelines.

The latter has undergone surgery for an adductor injury and could be ruled out until 2027, so Franjo Ivanovic is expected to lead the home side's attack.

Still struggling with a hamstring problem, Ecuadorian wing-back Jhoanner Chavez is also a doubt.

While veteran playmaker Florian Thauvin has created the most chances across the Champions League's opening three matchdays (15), Como star Paz has been directly involved in five goals.

Douvikas has scored in all three of the Lariani's league-phase appearances, so they are both integral parts of the Fabregas plan.

The Catalan coach will still be without Moise Kean, Trevoh Chalobah, Jesus Rodriguez and Assane Diao due to injury, while Jayden Addai is a major doubt.

Sometimes rotated with Chelsea loanee Robert Sanchez, goalkeeper Jean Butez recently replaced Robin Risser of Lens in the France squad.

Risser; Aguilar, Baidoo, Todibo; Abdulhamid, Cuisance, Haidara, Udol; Thauvin, Sotoca; Ivanovic

Butez; Smolcic, Kempf, Ramon, Valle; Perrone, Ricci; Da Cunha, Paz, Baturina; Douvikas

Although the sample size is small, Como tend to start sharply in Europe, having scored first - and during the first half - in all three of their Champions League matches.

The Lariani also possess a potency that Lens simply cannot withstand, so they will move up to nine points and leave their hosts stranded on three.

#1735. FIFA Slaps Real Madrid, Atletico Madrid With 1-Year Transfer Bans

Home » Home 2 » FIFA Slaps Real Madrid, Atletico Madrid With 1-Year Transfer Bans

The ban will start from the July transfer window this year and finish with the January transfer market in 2017.

Atletico were also fined 900,000 Swiss francs (820,000 euros) and Real 360,000 (330,000 euros).

“The two clubs were found to have violated several provisions concerning the international transfer and first registration of minor players as well as other relevant provisions with regard to the registration and participation of certain players in competitions,” said a FIFA statement.

Barcelona has just ended a one year ban for similar reasons.

Real and Atletico were “issued with a reprimand and given 90 days in which to regularise the situation of all minor players concerned,” FIFA said. They can still sell players during the transfer ban.

FIFA said the alarm was raised over the two clubs by FIFA’s Transfer Matching System and its disciplinary committee completed the inquiry.

Under international football rules, players under 18 cannot be transferred to another country, except in limited circumstances. All transfers need the approval of a special FIFA committee.

“The investigations concerned minor players who were involved and participated in competitions with the clubs over various periods between 2007 and 2014 (Atletico Madrid) and between 2005 and 2014 (Real Madrid),” FIFA said.

The ban follows a similar sanction handed to European champions Barcelona, who were unable to register new players during 2015.

Barca were initially banned in April 2014, but managed to delay the sanction taking affect until the transfer windows in January and the summer 2015 by launching an ultimately unsuccessful appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS).

By delaying the ban, Barca managed to sign the likes of Luis Suarez and Ivan Rakitic in the summer of 2014 to propel them to a treble of La Liga, Champions League and Copa del Rey.

The news is just the latest institutional embarassment for Real Madrid just over a week after they appointed French legend Zinedine Zidane.

Madrid have sacked two Champions League winning coaches in Carlo Ancelotti and Rafael Benitez in the past seven months, as well as being thrown out of the Copa del Rey for fielding an ineligible player.

The sanction could also be bad news for the likes of Paris Saint-Germain and Manchester United, who had targeted Madrid stars Cristiano Ronaldo and Gareth Bale with Real highly unlikely to dispose of their best players without the chance to sign suitable replacements.

La Liga leaders Atletico Madrid’s usually hectic transfer policy will also be put on hold. However, Diego Simeone’s men look better placed to cope with the ban having invested heavily in young talent over the past year.

Neither Real no Atletico made an immediate comment on whether they would appeal.

#1731. Opinion: Insane Trent Alexander-Arnold Liverpool return moves one step closer, story out of Real Madrid hints at it

Trent Alexander-Arnold's future is up in the air right now. A move to Liverpool looks a lot more likely after recent comments out of Real Madrid.

Trent Alexander-Arnold didn't exactly shock the football world when he left Liverpool for Real Madrid in 2025 but it was certainly one of the biggest moves in recent times. A homegrown Reds deciding to move away from the club, using the end of his contract to sign for Los Blancos.

It's a story we've seen before. Twice, ridiculously enough.

Steve McManaman did it back in 1999 as one of the very first major players to take advantage of the Bosman ruling. Though, Liverpool were a bit of a mess at the time and certainly not looking capable of challenging for the top honours.

Michael Owen in 2004, however, was a massive blow. He didn't really leave on a free but entered the final year of his contract while refusing to sign a new one. That forced a cut-price move for Liverpool's most valuable player, who joined Real Madrid for a pittance.

Fast-forward to 2025 and Alexander-Arnold did exactly the same thing. The Reds got a small fee for a fraction of his value and lost him to Madrid.

And yet, there's a sense that he might be the first of the three to actually head back the other way. Especially as it might just suit all parties.

Trent Alexander-Arnold to LiverpoolAlexander-Arnold joined Real Madrid with dreams of the Ballon d'Or. It doesn't feel too much to say that it's all turned into a nightmare. The Scouser just doesn't play. He's appeared in just six of a possible 10 La Liga fixtures, starting a mere three of those. It's 266 minutes total out of a possible 900. And now Jose Mourinho is making it clear that this is purely preference. There's competition for places at right-back and Alexander-Arnold is not first choice. Or second. "[The situation with Alexander-Arnold] hurts me, said Mourinho. "Our squad planning was to have 2 players in each position, and now I'm playing a 3rd guy in their place [Fede Valverde], and that really makes me sad.

Alexander-Arnold joined Real Madrid with dreams of the Ballon d'Or. It doesn't feel too much to say that it's all turned into a nightmare.

The Scouser just doesn't play. He's appeared in just six of a possible 10 La Liga fixtures, starting a mere three of those. It's 266 minutes total out of a possible 900.

And now Jose Mourinho is making it clear that this is purely preference. There's competition for places at right-back and Alexander-Arnold is not first choice. Or second.

"[The situation with Alexander-Arnold] hurts me, said Mourinho.

"Our squad planning was to have 2 players in each position, and now I'm playing a 3rd guy in their place [Fede Valverde], and that really makes me sad.

"In this very specific situation, I think it's better for the team to play Fede there. I consider Fede a more offensive right-back than the other two right now.

"We explained this situation to Trent and [Denzel] Dumfries, and they both accepted it as they understood it's what best for the team right now.

Maybe everyone will play eventually but right now it's Alexander-Arnold who's missing out. Dumfries has started five of their 10 La Liga fixtures, playing in eight.

Understandably, then, speculation continues that Alexander-Arnold will leave the club and his reputation will absolutely develop intense interest in him from major clubs. But once you look at the elite clubs in need of a right-back, one stands out: Liverpool.

Jeremie Frimpong, essentially signed as Alexander-Arnold's replacement, has not worked out and they don't currently have a natural right-back. Ronald Araujo plays there but he's really a centre-back, even if he's playing very well.

His attacking output is minimal - a dramatic difference to when Alexander-Arnold was there.

Mourinho's admittance that the player is out of the team because he's just not preferred there is a proper admittance that Alexander-Arnold is surplus to requirements. Real Madrid won't let that situation continue, given his wages and value.

A move is getting closer, then. And it's to Liverpool that makes the most sense.

#1730. Portsmouth vs Swansea City - prediction, team news, lineups

By Calum Burrowes | 02 Nov 2026 15:44, Last updated: 02 Nov 2026 16:50

Portsmouth and Swansea City meet at Fratton Park on Tuesday night, with both sides looking to build on their encouraging starts to the 2026-27 Championship campaign.

Pompey were held to a 0-0 draw by recently relegated Burnley at the weekend, while the Swans returned to winning ways in emphatic fashion by thrashing Blackburn Rovers 4-0 at the Swansea.com Stadium.

Since securing promotion to the Championship in May 2024 and successfully avoiding a return to League One across the last two seasons, John Mousinho has continued to oversee steady progress at Portsmouth, with their recent results suggesting the manager has once again taken his side up another level.

Pompey were held to a goalless draw by Burnley, who were competing in the Premier League just a few months ago, although the result offered a mixed assessment of their performance, highlighting both their defensive strengths and their continued struggles in attack.

After 13 Championship matches, Portsmouth sit in the top half of the table, having recorded five wins, four draws and four defeats to collect 19 points and establish a healthy cushion over the relegation zone.

However, Saturday's stalemate against Burnley, who have now gone 22 matches without a win at Turf Moor, underlined their ability to remain organised at the back while also exposing their wastefulness in the final third, where a lack of cutting edge continues to undermine their efforts.

Their tally of 16 goals is the lowest of any side in the top half and among the poorest returns in the division, making their attacking output an area Mousinho will be eager to improve as he approaches his 200th match in charge of Pompey.

As for Swansea City, they make the trip to Fratton Park enjoying their best start to a Championship season since being relegated from the Premier League more than eight years ago, despite heading into the weekend on the back of consecutive defeats.

The Swans travelled to Loftus Road a week before Halloween and were thrashed 5-0 by Queens Park Rangers, following an earlier defeat to former Premier League side West Ham United, with their place at the top of the table subsequently taken by Middlesbrough.

Despite entering the weekend inside the top two, Vitor Matos and his Swansea side were determined to end their brief losing run at the earliest opportunity, and they did so in emphatic fashion by putting four goals past Blackburn Rovers in South Wales.

First-half strikes from Stephen Eustaquio, Joseph Opoku and Filip Lissah put the Swans firmly in control before Ross Stewart added a fourth shortly before the hour mark, completing a superb response to the heaviest defeat of Matos's reign and matching their biggest victory under the Portuguese manager.

That eighth win of the campaign, alongside two draws and three defeats, leaves Swansea second in the standings, just two points behind the league leaders as they look to maintain their promotion push.

Looking to build on their encouraging start to the campaign, Portsmouth could name an unchanged side for their second away fixture in four days after coming through the weekend's draw without any fresh injury concerns.

However, Mousinho will remain without Connor Ogilvie, Keshi Anderson, John Swift, Luke Brooke-Smith and Colby Bishop, who are all unavailable.

As for Swansea, Matos would ideally like to retain the starting XI that performed so impressively against Blackburn, but he may be forced into at least one change.

Eustaquio, who opened the scoring in Saturday's 4-0 victory, is a doubt after being forced off 17 minutes from time with a groin injury.

Adam Idah replaced the Canadian midfielder during the weekend win, but Matos may favour a more like-for-like alternative when selecting his side for Tuesday's trip to Hampshire.

Cameron Burgess, Ronald and Moussa Kounfolo Yeo remain unavailable for the Welsh visitors.

#1729. Sampdoria swept aside by rampant Napoli – are the Partenopei on course for their first Scudetto in 26 years?

Home » Home 2 » Sampdoria swept aside by rampant Napoli – are the Partenopei on course for their first Scudetto in 26 years?

Dries Mertens celebrating with his team-mates on the touchline after his decisive goal in the 4-2 victory at Sampdoria is typical of the spirit and togetherness that has seen Napoli storm to the top of the Serie A title. It was in dedication to Chelsea loanee Nathaniel Chabolah who recently lost his mother a a nice touch to show that there is much more to life than football, even though they have put themselves in a wonderful position to end Juventusa dominance and end a 26-year wait for the Scudetto.

Five straight wins have put Maurizio Sarria s team two points clear at the top, with the former Empoli manager breathing a new lease of life throughout a team that have always looked capable of competing for the title, yet ultimately fallen short when the pressure to deliver grew. He has transformed the entire dynamics of how Napoli play, with clinical attacking movement combined with a rock-solid defence within a 4-3-3 system that is getting the very best from the players at his disposal. This seasona s statistics proved that point; Napoli are far and away the highest scorers in Serie A this season, while only Inter Milan and Juventus have a better defensive record. Just one defeat in the twenty league games since the opening day loss at Sassuolo is another illustration of just how good Napoli have been this season, with the crushing 4-0 win at AC Milan in early October a sign of what the Partenopei are truly capable of.

Juventus were always likely to be favourites for the Scudetto on Coral and any other football odds site as their dominance of Italian football threatens to extend into its fifth season, so it is perhaps refreshing from a purista s perspective that Napoli have emerged as real contenders to challenge the Bianconeri. Massimo Allegria s side have stormed up the table in ominous fashion following a surprisingly slow start to the season, with eleven straight victories serving a serious warning to Napoli that they will make them fight all the way for the 2015/2016 Serie A title. It remains to be seen how Sarri and his team handle the pressure of having Juventus breathing down their necks, but the fact they have scored twelve goals in their last three games would indicate that

Some may have been surprised by Gonzalo Higuaina s decision to swap Real Madrid for Naples in the summer of 2013, but the 28-year-old has become one of the most feared strikers in Italy. The Argentine international has formed a wonderful strikeforce at the front of a three-man attack, with Jose Callejon and Lorenzo Insigne adding searing pace and skill on either side of a frontman who has made a career from being a true predator inside the box.

Twenty-one games in as many Serie A games this season puts him amongst the most in-form strikers in world football, with his clinical finish which opened the scoring against Sampdoria proving just how good he has been in front of goal. It is the sort of purple patch that any striker worth their salt would dream to be in; Coral have unsurprisingly backed Higuain as favourite to score in their next game against Sarria s former employers Empoli who have kept just one clean sheet from their last five league fixtures. Napoli will need Higuain to carry his rich vein of form throughout the rest of the season if they are to have any chance of maintaining their wonderful pace and sprint clear of the chasing pack.

Napoli have won many admirers across Europe for the quality of football they have played this season, but it remains to be seen if they have the mentality to pass the acid test and keep the momentum going between now and the end of the season. Recent history would suggest that their chances are not great; the Partenopei, then managed by Walter Mazzarri, put themselves in a wonderful position in 2012/2013, only to finish runners-up behind Juventus as the odd slip at the wrong times proved costly in their pursuit of Juventus. A number of third-placed finishes would also suggest that Napoli have lacked the mentality and guile to end their long wait for a Scudetto, but there is real excitement in Naples that the current crop of players have what it takes to stop the Old Lady from making it five titles in a row.

#1728. EPL Prepares for Most Exciting Title Race in Years

Home » Home 2 » EPL Prepares for Most Exciting Title Race in Years

Now that all of the top four English Premier League teams have had a chance to play each other, we find ourselves looking at one of the most wide open title races in recent memory. As of this writing, the league leaders are only separated by a mere six points. With the exception of Manchester City, we could very well see a new face hoisting the Premier League trophy at the end of the season.

For much of the year, it looked like Arsenal would be in the running for its first league title in more than a decade. With the Gunners’ recent victory against Leicester City, they are very much back in the conversation. Danny Welbeck returned to the pitch for the first time this season and made an immediate impact for Arsene Wenger’s squad, scoring the last-minute, game-winning goal to propel the team to within two points of the top spot. Given that even more key players are set to return to action for Arsenal in the coming months, this is easily the best shot they have had of winning a championship since their undefeated 2003-04 season.

Another surprise team that certainly deserves its own mention is Tottenham Hotspur. Following the club’s controversial defeat of Manchester City, the Spurs sit in second place, a mere two points behind Leicester City and ahead of Arsenal on goal differential. Tottenham have yet to win a title in the Premier League era and they have not won an English championship since 1961. The team has done a superb job of backing up star striker Harry Kane with a glut of promising young players, and their goal tally only helps to reinforce the wisdom behind the strategy of manager Mauricio Pochettino.

Meanwhile, Manchester City is still hoping to snag its third title as something of a swan song for exiting manager Manuel Pellegrini. It was recently announced that the club had hired Pep Guardiola . from Bayern Munich to take charge of the team beginning with next season. Thus, Pellegrini has been forced to endure the rest of the campaign as a dead man walking. Despite the impending exit of Pellegrini, City are still in the race for the Premier League title in addition to both the F.A. Cup and Champions League. Theoretically, the club could pull off a treble, if it can manage a solid string of performances during the final half of the season.

At the beginning of the season, it was expected that the usual suspects would once again dominate the league. Many predicted the reigning champs at Chelsea to repeat their success. However, a shocking season has seen the team part ways with controversial manager Jose Mourinho and struggle to remain in the top half of the tables with hopes of a Champions League spot dashed long ago.

For the first time in years, there’s a chance to see a completely new team win the league. No matter which club you support, there’s no denying that this has made for one of the most thrilling contests in recent memory. In a league where money talks, small fish like Leicester City are surprising everyone, and we can only hope that this means a new era of parity for the Premier League.
