Good afternoon and welcome to live coverage of Everton vs Manchester United from Hill Dickinson Stadium. The hosts have made a creditable start on the field but four points from their opening two games cannot gloss over the discontent fostered by the owners and executives because of the credibility gap between their talk about recruitment and their paltry achievements.

The fact that their comeback against Bournemouth to earn a draw last week was achieved with Beto, Tim Iroegbunum and Iliman Ndiaye on the field and all three have now been sold with only Jack Grealish returning on loan to compensate tells its own story.

Speak to supporters and it is emblematic of ownership, they fear, who are prioritising Roma and view the Hill Dickinson as a terrific multisport and concert venue with a heritage football club attached. The bullishness of Angus Kinnear, the chief executive, rings hollower with each pronouncement and it is little wonder that the fans are so disenchanted.

David Moyes will not walk away but once again he has been sent into the fray against teams with £250m midfields armed with a spud gun. Having said that, we should not underestimate his capacity to rally the old “dogs of war” spirit even if the crowd is still yearning more for a “school of science” revival.

Manchester United won on their first visit to the Hill Dickinson last season when Benjamin Sesko came off the bench to score the only goal of the game and give Michael Carrick a fifth win in six league games as caretaker manager. They were far more fluid in their forward play during the victory over Ipswich last week but it was against an error-stricken defence and they continued to be as worryingly open at the back as they had been against Hull City in the opening round of fixtures with Luke Shaw and Lisandro Martínez having brain fades.

Shaw is a doubt today, along with Mason Mount, while Amad Diallo, Matthijs de Ligt, Carlos Baleba and Manuel Ugarte have all been ruled out. Only Christian Norgaard is absent for Everton but so thin is their squad, they will cast covetous glances at Man Utd’s bench, not least at Joshua Zirkzee who was the subject of a very late rejected bid on deadline day.

#1662. CorSera: Inacio then Tresoldi – Milan’s plans to level up the squad outlined

The derby victory against Inter has brought a sense of excitement to AC Milan, and plans are being drawn up for a potentially busy January.

This morning’s edition of Corriere della Sera (via MilanNews) writes that Gerry Cardinale was among the happiest in attendance on Saturday night. The RedBird boss continues to reiterate his desire to bring Milan back to the top, and for this reason he’s ready to strengthen the team in January.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Not only that, but he is ready and willing to make signings that make a guaranteed difference in terms of quality, unlike last winter when the only reinforcement to arrive was Niclas Füllkrug from West Ham (now the Bundesliga top scorer).

The first move is the hiring of Markus Krosche, who will officially become the new Head of Football in the coming weeks. Milan lack someone in this role, having left it vacant since the failed summer pursuit of the German, but Cardinale didn’t give up and has got his man.

In January, the priority remains a central defender, and Gonçalo Inacio’s name remains at the top of the list. The Rossoneri are ready to try again for the Sporting CP centre-back, who – like Krösche – was pursued in the summer too.

Then there’s the mystery of Ramos’s replacement in attack, as Francesco Camarda is struggling to find playing time. So it’s possible the young striker could be sent out on loan to play consistently and continue his development.

A new centre-forward would replace him, alternating with Gonçalo Ramos. The dream would be Nicolò Tresoldi, but bringing him to Milan in the winter transfer window seems nearly impossible. The matter will likely be discussed again in the summer.

#1661. Newcastle vs. Everton lineups confirmed: Grealish, Branthwaite, Elanga decisions made for Premier League clash

By Oliver Thomas | 02 Nov 2026 18:49, Last updated: 02 Nov 2026 19:06

Jack Grealish has officially been left out of Everton’s squad for tonight’s Premier League clash against Newcastle United at St James’ Park.

It was reported hours before kickoff that the 31-year-old winger would not travel with David Moyes's squad as he is 'not fit' to feature for the Toffees.

Grealish is absent for the second successive game having previously missed Everton's EFL Cup fourth-round home win over the Magpies on Thursday due to a 'breach of club discipline'.

On a positive note, Jarrad Branthwaite is fit to start in central defence after missing the last two matches due to serving his concussion protocol.

Branthwaite is one of two changes made to Moyes's first XI from last week, with midfielder Harrison Armstrong also returning as Tyler Dibling and Hayden Hackney both drop down to the substitutes' bench.

The return of Branthwaite will see him start alongside James Tarkowski at centre-back, with Jake O'Brien expected to move over to right-back.

Left-back Vitaliy Mykolenko completes the back four, while Armstrong, James Garner and Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall will all line up in midfield.

Tyrique George will continue on the left flank in the absence of Grealish, while Merlin Rohl is set to move further forward and operate on the right side of midfield, with Thierno Barry leading the line once again.

As for Newcastle, head coach Matthias Jaissle has also made just two changes to his Magpies side following the 3-1 EFL Cup defeat at the Hill Dickinson Stadium five days ago.

Anthony Elanga will start his first match for Newcastle in almost two months since recovering from injury, with the winger taking the place of Jacob Murphy on the right side of attack.

Joelinton, who was involved in a heated altercation with Tarkowski towards the end of Thursday's contest, is also recalled at the expense of Jacob Ramsey and will link up with Nico Gonzalez and Joe Willock in midfield.

William Osula is fit to continue up front, while Harvey Barnes will make his 100th Premier League appearance for the Magpies and is also just one goal away from his 100th career goal.

Dan Burn will captain Newcastle and will be joined in four-man defence by Amar Dedic, Fabian Schar and Lewis Hall, protecting goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek.

Newcastle United starting lineup: Hornicek; Dedic, Schar, Burn, Hall; Joelinton, Gonzalez; Elanga, Willock, Barnes; Osula

Subs: Pope, Botman, Bamba, Wissa, Thiaw, Steur, Toure, Murphy, Ramsey

Everton starting lineup: Pickford; O'Brien, Tarkowski, Branthwaite, Mykolenko; Garner, Armstrong; Rohl, Dewsbury-Hall, George; Barry

Subs: Travers, Maitland-Niles, Dibling, Keane, Johnson, Norgaard, Alcaraz, Hackney, Graham

#1660. Report: Julian Ward makes contact with exciting left-back, he could replace Kerkez

Julian Ward has reportedly made contact to sign an exciting left-back for Liverpool.

There is a new man in charge at Anfield, although he is hardly a stranger. Julian Ward is back, and he already knows what it takes to succeed as Liverpool's sporting director.

His previous spell in the role was a fruitful one, but disagreements with Jurgen Klopp over the club's long-term direction ultimately led to his resignation. Ward officially departed in the summer of 2023, only to return just over a year later following Klopp's announcement that he would leave Liverpool.

Since then, Ward has quietly worked behind the scenes, contributing to recruitment and helping shape the club's plans. Now, he has the opportunity to step back into the spotlight and lead Liverpool's next chapter.

Liverpool want to reinforce the left-back positionWhen Milos Kerkez arrived at the club, he was regarded as the best young player in his position not only in the Premier League but in European football. Kerkez didn't have it easy, entering the club at a horrific time with everyone reeling from the tragedy of Diogo Jota's death. Then came a brutal season as Arne Slot struggled to get the best out of his team. In that time, Kerkez was often unfairly labelled as a scapegoat and received a lot of harsh criticism that was simply not warranted. Now with his former coach at Bournemouth Andoni Iraola at the club, it's very apparent that the Hungarian is getting back to his best. That doesn't mean that he won't be getting anymore competition. Julian Ward is ready to bring someone in who could challenge and potentially replace him as well.

When Milos Kerkez arrived at the club, he was regarded as the best young player in his position not only in the Premier League but in European football.

Kerkez didn't have it easy, entering the club at a horrific time with everyone reeling from the tragedy of Diogo Jota's death. Then came a brutal season as Arne Slot struggled to get the best out of his team.

In that time, Kerkez was often unfairly labelled as a scapegoat and received a lot of harsh criticism that was simply not warranted.

Now with his former coach at Bournemouth Andoni Iraola at the club, it's very apparent that the Hungarian is getting back to his best.

That doesn't mean that he won't be getting anymore competition. Julian Ward is ready to bring someone in who could challenge and potentially replace him as well.

Liverpool make contact with El Hadji Malick Diouf's agentThere's an exciting move on the horizon for Liverpool. According to journalist Khadim Diakhate writing on X, the Reds are interested in signing Brentford's Senegalese left-back. Diouf has caught the eye ever since he came into the Premier League, and he's also established himself as a regular member of Senegal's national team. Brentford signed him for £40m from West Ham United in the summer. However, according to Diakhate Liverpool are already sniffing around for his services with the journalist claiming that the Reds have already made contact with Diouf's representatives over a potential transfer. #1658. Pioli discusses current Milan team, relationship with Ibrahimovic, Scudetto win and Moreira

Stefano Pioli shared some more insight on his time as AC Milan head coach, including the impact of Zlatan Ibrahimovic, Rafael Leao and others.

Pioli was a guest on Sky Calcio Club after Juventus 2-0 Napoli last night, and he revisited the 2021-22 Scudetto win, discussing some of the characteristics of the players, and also drawing comparisons with some current squad members. MilanVibes relayed his words.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Firstly, the coach was asked about if he saw a bit of Rafael Leao in Diego Moreira, given the Belgian was the hero of the derby on Saturday night with one goal and two assists.

“I saw him against Sassuolo too, and he impressed me. He and Rabiot are really strong. Milan played a great match, Maignan made a great save… but with their starting eleven, they’re a really strong team. When Amorim made a few more substitutions, they struggled more.

“It took them a while to get to this point because they had players arriving, probably with some problems, and it takes time to find their rhythm and fitness.

“The results are showing. Modric also still has some important strength. Gonçalo Ramos is doing a great job for the team and is a very good player.”

The discussion about Milan inevitably brought them back to the team that won the league title in 2022. Pioli explained how the playing system was built around the characteristics of the players available, with particular attention to the defensive line and the ability to sustain aggressive football.

“A coach’s skill lies in adapting to a player’s characteristics. At AC Milan, I had players who got lost defending deep. I like that style of play, but it was the best one for those players.

“Kalulu and Tomori also allowed us to take risks. If you want to stay high up the pitch, you need to have significant intensity; anything in between doesn’t work.”

Pioli commented on Leao again, who reached the peak of his powers under the Italian, but also admitted that after the Scudetto not everything went as he would have hoped.

The Scudetto year was devastating. I’ve seen few players of that level. Then he wasn’t, and we weren’t, good. Because when you win, it’s because something special is created in the team. Paolo [Maldini], Ricky [Massara], and I weren’t good – and neither was he – at maintaining and further raising his level.

“He certainly has important qualities. The coach has to understand the players. Rafa is a good player who needs to be encouraged in a certain way.”

During the segment, the background on Roma’s interest also emerged. The Giallorossi contacted Pioli, but at that point the coach had already received an offer from Al Nassr.

“There were times when everyone called me. Even Roma, but I had just received my contract with Al Nassr and I couldn’t break my word.

“I don’t regret going to Saudi Arabia. I wanted to gain experience abroad after my years with AC Milan. The financial aspect and the opportunity to coach Cristiano Ronaldo also played a role.

“If you don’t coach him, you don’t understand how great he is. He’s a champion, obsessed with preparing to score goals. He’s very respectful.”

Pioli spoke about Zlatan Ibrahimovic and Cristiano Ronaldo, two of the biggest profiles that he has had to manage in his career to date.

“Cristiano and Zlatan have a very similar relationship: ‘You’re clear with me and I respect you, if you’re not clear with me, it’s no good.’ I’ve always based our relationship on clarity and sincerity.

“It’s clear that with Zlatan and Cristiano, if you tell them, ‘Look, you’re not playing tomorrow, or you’ll play 60 minutes tomorrow,’ and then I’ll take you off, and you do it or you don’t, it makes a difference.

“I didn’t tell Zlatan something once, but I didn’t tell him because in the rush, I think during the Covid period, we were playing every three days. At the end of the first half it was 0-0, then in 10 minutes we scored 2-3 goals, I don’t remember now…

“Anyway, I made three substitutions: I remember Zlatan, Calhanoglu, and another. So quick, but I hadn’t told Zlatan in advance… The next day [laughs]. he came to me… The good thing about Zlatan is that as soon as he gets over it, the next day it’s as if nothing had happened.”

When asked if Ibrahimovic frequently sulked, Pioli replied: “No, absolutely not. He’s great. But does he tell you? Yes, yes, and then with a tone…

“I always leave my office door open because I like to greet the players and see them. In fact, I had the office changed because I wanted it to be between the locker room and physiotherapy, which they have to go to every day anyway, so every day I greeted all the players, and they came in to see me.

“Every now and then I stopped them, but I didn’t stop them. That day, I didn’t expect Zlatan to come in. He came in and said, ‘I’ll speak today.’ You know, those chairs that move around, I danced for 2-3 minutes, but then it went away.”

Pioli also recalled his first meeting with the Swede, who arrived at Milanello at the end of January 2020 and undoubtedly played a key role in the resurgence.

“Ibrahimovic arrived at Milanello the first day. I waited for him there, and he arrived when it was dark. It was January, the end of January. I followed him in his training, but he also had a knee problem.

“He did a bit of treadmill work, then he came to my office, spoke to me a bit, and I explained to him how I wanted to use him on the pitch, technically and tactically. He said to me: ‘You’re the coach, I’m the player. You respect me, I’ll respect you.’ And that’s what happened.”

Pioli also spoke about the relationship between results and the team, explaining why it’s often more difficult for a coach to put a defeat behind him than to enjoy a victory.

“We coaches don’t enjoy victories because we immediately think about the next game. Defeat, however, stays with you. But what happened to me at Milan was incredibly emotional. Sackings, on the other hand, are difficult; you feel guilty.

“The one in Florence was even more difficult. I had returned with so much willpower and energy. I had returned with so much confidence, and it was a tough blow.”

Finally, a revelation about the possibility of becoming Italy’s coach. Pioli confirmed that he had been close to taking over the national team, but without going into details.

“I’ve touched on it, but not for very long. In our careers, we are the product of all the choices we make. Some are good, some aren’t.”

#1657. Barcelona head coach Hansi Flick discusses Alejandro Balde future amid exit reports

By Matt Law | 02 Nov 2026 19:07, Last updated: 02 Nov 2026 19:08

Barcelona head coach Hansi Flick has suggested that Alejandro Balde still has a future at Camp Nou despite his struggles during the 2026-27 campaign.

Flick said ahead of Barcelona's clash with Alaves on Saturday that Balde currently does not have "the confidence he needs to play".

“Balde doesn’t have the confidence he needs to play, the conviction to attack and press high. The full-backs are very important for us, in our style of play. He needs confidence to reach his best level," Flick told reporters.

Injuries for Xavi Espart, Jules Kounde, Andreas Christensen and Eric Garcia had seemingly opened the door for Balde to start against Alaves.

However, Joao Cancelo started at left-back, with Brian Farinas at right-back, while Frenkie de Jong featured in the middle of the defence.

Balde was instead used off the bench, playing the final 28 minutes of the league fixture.

The Spain international has only played 116 minutes of action for Barcelona this season, and there is currently a host of speculation surrounding his future.

Manchester United are in the market for a left-back and could reignite their interest in the 23-year-old when the winter window opens for business.

Balde could potentially start Barcelona's Champions League fixture against Aston Villa on Tuesday, but it is more likely that he will again feature on the bench.

Flick has suggested that Balde is still in his plans moving forward, with the German determined to "help" the defender "regain his confidence".

“What’s happening to him is normal; when you don’t play often, you lack confidence. I see him training well, but we have to decide what’s best for the team, and Joao Cancelo is in great form,” Flick told reporters during his press conference.

“When I say he lacks confidence, I know it can affect him, and I spoke to him after the last press conference. I respect him a lot; he’s young, but he’s a great person and a very hard worker. I’ll help him regain his confidence.”

Balde has made 172 appearances for Barcelona in all competitions since breaking into their first team, scoring three goals and registering 21 assists.

An Ohio high school soccer referee was left seriously injured after being inexplicably tackled by a player during a playoff game this week.

The barely-believable incident occurred during a district matchup between New Philadelphia and Steubenville on Tuesday night.

New Philadelphia's 2-1 victory was overshadowed by the ugly scenes when the official was bodychecked to the ground by one of the players.

The offending player, who appeared to be a member of Steubenville's team, was seemingly left frustrated after one of his teammates was shown a red card.

In viral footage shared by Bob Greenburg on X, the unassuming referee could be seen walking away after booking the teammate when the player inexplicably ran into the back of him.

The unidentified player was captured charging at the running official before driving head-first into the referee's midriff and leaving him sprawled on the turf.

A high school soccer referee was left injured after being tackled to the ground by a player

The official was taken to hospital where he is being treated for broken ribs and a collapsed lung, according to TMZ.

The Ohio High School Athletic Association is yet to announce a formal punishment to the player over the shocking incident but it vowed that the consequences will be significant - and most definitely worse than a red card.

'The OHSAA is waiting for a response from the school to announce the discipline that the school will take against the student-athlete, which will determine if the OHSAA will issue additional penalties,' a spokesperson for the organization told The Daily Mail.

'The school has indicated that punishment will be significant, which the OHSAA agrees with. Physical violence against an official is among the most serious offenses that a coach, player or fan can commit and the OHSAA will pursue this to the fullest extent possible.'

'The Steubenville City Schools is aware of the incident involving a student and a game official following a recent athletic contest,' a spokesperson for the Steubenville Board of Education told The Daily Mail in a statement.

'The District worked collaboratively with the Ohio High School Athletic Association (OHSAA) to review the matter and ensure it was addressed appropriately.

The offending player was seen charging at the official before driving head-first into him

'The District remains committed to maintaining high standards of sportsmanship, respect, and safety at all athletic events.'

New Philadelphia traveled to Steubenville for the Division III level clash on Tuesday with the two schools separated by just 60 miles.

Thanks to their win, New Philadelphia will now face Dover in the District Final on Thursday evening with a place in the Regional Semifinals on the line.

Steubenville and their reckless player, meanwhile, were eliminated from the playoffs by Tuesday night's result.

Barcelona are reportedly taking a close interest in Jordan Arnolin, but the Estoril centre-back is also attracting attention in France and the Premier League.

Barcelona are not only looking to sign established players to strengthen their defence. The Catalan club, leader in LaLiga, are also scouting young European talents, and according to Portuguese newspaper Record, they sent a representative to the Estadio do Dragao on Saturday to watch 18-year-old Arnolin.

The interest comes as Barcelona have spent several months trying to strengthen their back line. The sporting department is working on several profiles, with the aim of finding a centre-back who can give Hansi Flick more guarantees.

The name of Inter Milan stalwart Alessandro Bastoni has been mentioned insistently in recent months, most recently by Sky Sports. The Italy international would be an especially expensive operation, however, and Inter have no reason to make his departure easy. Against that backdrop, a young player with high potential is another route for the Barcelona hierarchy, and Arnolin fits that logic.

Barcelona will have to contend with two other suitors. According to Record, Lille and Brighton and Hove Albion also sent representatives to the Dragao to monitor the young Portuguese.

For Lille, the move would fit a well-established recruitment policy of backing high-potential players who can take a step up and increase in value. The northern French club have regularly used that model to bring in players who are not yet well known to the wider public. Brighton are a far stronger financial rival, with greater resources than Lille and their own reputation for finding talent. Their ability to attract young players and offer them exposure in the Premier League is another argument in their favour.

Lille face a stiff challenge. Barcelona have a sporting and media pull that is unmatched, and even though Arnolin would probably not walk straight into Flick’s starting line-up, joining the Catalan club would be hard for an 18-year-old to turn down.

Lille do have one strong argument in playing time. With heavy competition in the Barcelona squad, particularly at centre-back, the young Portuguese could have to wait for first-team chances, while a gradual path to the Lille first team looks easier to envisage.

The financial side remains a factor, too. Brighton have more room for manoeuvre, and Barcelona keep considerable economic strength and international appeal, despite their well-known budget constraints. Lille will probably have to rely on their sporting project and their ability to support the defender’s progress.

Another element could complicate negotiations. Arnolin has just signed his first professional contract with Estoril, running until June 2029, so the club are under no pressure to sell. Lille have a card to play, but they will need to be convincing to beat two very serious competitors.

#1650. Manchester United targeting £70 million Newcastle star as January transfer hopes fade

Barnaby Lane is a highly experienced sports writer who has written for The Times, FourFourTwo Magazine, Sports Illustrated, TalkSPORT, and Business Insider. Over the years, he's had the pleasure of interviewing some of the biggest names in world sport, including Usain Bolt, Rafael Nadal, Christian Pulisic, and more.

Manchester United remain interested in signing Newcastle United defender Lewis Hall, but securing his services could prove difficult after the left-back committed his future to the Magpies.

The England international was among United’s defensive targets during the summer transfer window.

However, Newcastle refused to entertain his departure, and his new contract has strengthened their position ahead of any potential negotiations.

Despite those obstacles, United continue to view Hall as a long-term option at left-back.

According to ⁠Football Insider, Manchester United would likely need to pay at least £70 million to persuade Newcastle to part with the 22-year-old.

Transfer correspondent Pete O’Rourke reports that Hall remains high on United’s list of targets, with the club continuing to monitor his situation.

O’Rourke explained: “They do like Lewis Hall and see him as somebody who could come in there and become a mainstay for them at left back for the foreseeable future in that side.”

Hall has since signed a contract extension that keeps him at St James’ Park until 2031. That agreement puts Newcastle in a strong negotiating position, meaning United would likely need to make a substantial offer to have any chance of completing a deal.

Newcastle regard Hall as an important part of their plans and are under no immediate pressure to sell the defender.

His performances for club and country have enhanced his reputation, while his long-term contract gives the Magpies greater control over his future.

Although United have continued to track the situation, a January departure is reportedly not expected. A move next summer appears more plausible, although Newcastle’s stance could make negotiations difficult then as well.

Hall is also believed to be settled at Newcastle, so United would need both clubs to reach an agreement and the player to remain open to the switch.

United’s interest reflects their desire to strengthen at left-back and find a long-term option for the position. Hall’s age, Premier League experience and potential make him an attractive candidate.

However, a fee exceeding £70 million would represent a significant investment, particularly with Newcastle having little incentive to negotiate a sale.

United may therefore have to consider alternative targets if the Magpies refuse to lower their demands.

#1649. Villa end goal drought to finally give Emery’s new era lift-off

Unai Emery is building Aston Villa 2.0 and this was a night when his new kids on the block produced clear signs of lift-off for the next chapter.

Emery always springs into life on European nights and his reconstructed team secured their first win and goals of the season to leave Villa’s 1,700 fans singing in the rain.

Ten summer signings have arrived during a summer of upheaval, which included plenty of high-profile departures after the club’s Europa League triumph in May.

Yet this was an evening that will have further energised Emery on his return to the Champions League.

Nicolas Jackson, Zion Suzuki and João Gomes embody this new Villa team and all stood out here in Bruges.

Record £65m signing Jackson’s fine individual goal proved to be the winner to settle a chaotic, absorbing contest with the Belgian Pro League champions.

Jackson adds a third for Aston Villa after Sommer comes rushing out of his box! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/HZ1x3BkfK0

Suzuki, the £30m replacement for Emiliano Martínez, has clear presence in goal and he is Villa’s version of former Manchester City goalkeeper Ederson with his wide array of passing.

Gomes was also industrious in midfield to recover from what was a nightmarish debut at Brighton, where he was sent off after 40 minutes.

Despite all the changes to this team, talismanic captain John McGinn remains essential to Villa. He became their all-time leading goalscorer in major European competitions with his 12th goal and led by example again, as he has done so many times.

McGinn strikes to put Villa ahead in Bruges! 💥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/FJnuxSwYwo

There were also hints of a strong defensive partnership developing between Pau Torres and Victor Lindelof, following the sale of Ezri Konsa to Arsenal last month.

“Fantastic, fantastic,” purred Emery at one point in the second half from the technical area, and Villa’s season now appears up and running.

Emery said: “This was another step forward and I am so happy and thankful for this. The old players need to keep our standards high and show everyone this is the only way we can achieve the process and reach our targets.

“It’s very important to start the Champions League with three points and hopefully this will give us confidence for the league. We are improving and we must work hard – it is the only way.”

Although Emery has established a reputation as the Europa League king, winning that trophy five times, this competition has proved more difficult to master.

His best run was reaching the semi-finals in the 2021-22 season, when his Villarreal side lost to Liverpool.

It remains a tournament in which he is desperate to make an impression, with Villa returning to Champions League duty here for the first time since their thrilling encounter with Paris St-Germain in April 2025.

Only five of that starting XI from the second leg of the quarter-final remain and one of them, midfielder Amadou Onana, is out until next year after sustaining a serious knee injury at the World Cup with Belgium.

With European heavyweights Barcelona, PSG and Borussia Dortmund to come in the league phase, this always felt like a game Villa probably needed to win.

They had only managed one shot on target so far this season before arriving in this historic city, but scored three goals before half-time.

Their opener came against the run of play in the 11th minute, with McGinn casually finding the corner after a lung-bursting run from Torres. McGinn has overtaken former Villa striker Ollie Watkins at the top of the club’s continental goalscoring charts.

Brugge briefly wobbled but were level eight minutes later when Hugo Vetlesen swept home from 10 yards, capitalising on space in the penalty box.

Vetlesen draws Club Brugge level against Aston Villa! ⚡📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/4ZYwPcMHim

Villa were back in front less than 160 seconds later, with Gomes teeing up Emiliano Buendía for an easy finish. Gomes was released in the box by a clever backheel from Jackson.

Buendia restores Villa's lead just minutes after Club Brugge's equaliser, and Unai Emery is LOVING it! 🙌📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/h2WGkwkTI1

Two minutes before half-time Yann Sommer, Club Brugge’s new goalkeeper, then had a severe rush of blood to the head by racing from his goal to almost the halfway line in an attempt to intercept Torres’s long pass.

Jackson edged the ball past him and held off a defender to calmly slot into the empty net. He underlined in many moments why Emery has pursued him for so long, after the pair established a strong rapport at Villarreal.

Villa appeared relatively comfortable in the second half until Aaron Wan-Bissaka was judged to have handled a cross from Joaquin Seys, after referee Sandro Schärer was advised by VAR to review the incident on his TV monitor.

It was a simple decision and Nicolò Tresoldi put away the penalty to stir life back into the home supporters.

Club Brugge are back in it from the penalty spot after Wan-Bissaka's handball! 👀📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/pEanRJvimu

Villa defended resolutely as time began to tick away with Suzuki providing authority in goal. The first Japanese goalkeeper to play in the Champions League also produced a number of routine saves in a nervy finish.

This was a promising night for a new Villa era.

Full-time scenes in Bruges as Aston Villa get their Champions League campaign off to a winning start! 👏📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nYwtiQ6Xs7

Villa are defending with six at the back as midfield and defence merge into one. There are seconds remaining as Suzuki punts the ball up field and there is the final whistle! Villa make a winning start to the 2026-27 Champions League.

Another cross from the right is met, this time, by Tresoldi, but his header has no bite and Suzuki gathers.

Torres heads another Siquet cross behind for a corner. Brugge load the box but none of their players are able to get a meaningful touch on the ball before Diakhon slips just as he looks to get a shot away from the left of the box.

Slightly less mature play from Gomes, though. He bundles Vermant over and earns a needless yellow card.

Really mature play by Hemmings. Looking to break away, he simply puts his body between man and ball, inviting the challenge and winning a foul.

Villa are working hard in their compact mid-block and Brugge are struggling to find a way through.

Leko sends on Vermant and Diakhon for Potts and Virgili.

Barkley is one lucky boy. Attempting to play out under pressure, the midfielder gives the ball straight to Virgili, who cannot sort out his feet before offloading to Tresoldi far too late. A big let-off for Villa.

Gomes goes close after driving through Brugge’s midfield. He really should, though, have played in a free McGinn at the back post. Moments later Bogarde fires another shot goalwards but Sommer gets to it.

Villa have wrestled control away from their opponents. McGinn’s teasing cross evades everyone and Alysson’s cross takes a deflection which goes behind for a corner which is not up to much.

Lee hauls down Hemmings which gives Villa the opportunity to slow the game down. McGinn flights a delivery in from the left but Brugge clear their lines.

The ball comes out to Alysson who jinks in from the right, tiptoeing through a crowd, desperate to get a shot away on his left foot, but Seys does well to track his man and smother the effort.

Vanakan and Velesen and replaced by Tsawa and Lemarechal.

Yet another dangerous Siquet cross rains in from the right and here it is taken off Tresoldi’s toes by the tip of Lindelof’s boot. The defender did brilliantly to clear his lines at full stretch.

Hemmings burst towards the by-line and his cross trickles across the face of goal. Alysson is waiting at the far post but Seys does well to shield the ball and win a free-kick.

Villa’s best chance at putting this game to bed will come on the counter. And here McGinn plays in Jackson whose one-vs-one effort is stopped by Sommer.

Virgili from the left, Siquet from the right. Threats are coming from both wings and Villa need to get their foot on the ball if they are to take the sting out of Brugge’s attack.

Instead they allow Vetlesen a yard of space and his long-range sighter stings the hands of Suzuki who turns behind for a corner.

Emery switches out Buendia, Kamara and Wan-Bissaka for Alysson, Barkley and Bogarde before the corner is taken, and Suzuki stops the eventual delivery on the line after the ball spun off the post!

Another Virgili cross threatens to carve Villa open but they just about clear their lines. Then it is Siquet who delivers, this time from the right, but his cross just evades Tresoldi and Mechele at the far post. The home fans are invested in this, they believe their side can grab an equaliser...

Villa have got their tails between their legs here. From a position of strength, they have allowed the momentum to swing in the hosts’ favour and it has been largely self-inflicted.

Maatsen has a chance to break free but cannot build a head of steam before he is stymied.

Club Brugge 2 Aston Villa 3 (Tresoldi pen) Suzuki dives to his right early and Tresoldi slides the ball into the opposite side of the net. Just the one goal in it now!

Brugge have averted their attention to their right hand side, Siquet and Forbs attacking in tandem. A dangerous cross from Forbs is met by Tresoldi but he cannot get the requisite contact on it. Seys collects the ball on the far side and fires a delivery into Wan-Bissaka and out for a corner. Replays show that it comes off the defenders hand ...and referee Scharer is sent to the screen. He wastes no time at the monitor and awards a spot kick!

Villa do appear pretty comfortable here, despite some frequent pressure from Club Brugge.

Pau Torres has been outstanding so far at the back for Unai Emery’s team.

This is also a night where Emery’s ‘new’ Villa are coming of age, with Nicolas Jackson, Zion Suzuki and Joao Gomes also impressive.

Virgili then darts in field from his starting perch on the left. Tresoldi backheels the ball back into his path but Virgili’s effort is snuffed out.

McGinn, sensing Virgili’s growing influence on the half, takes matters into his own hands and leaves one on the Spanish winger, Siquet’s free-kick from deep is aimed at Tresoldi but Suzuki is wise to it and sweeps up.

Unai Emery has the new kids on the block but this Aston Villa team are hangin’ tough.

This has been a pretty chaotic first-half on the return of the Champions League but Emery will be satisfied with what he has seen so far. It’s very much a case of step by step for his reshaped team, but they should see this game out now.

It’s been a shocking night for Club Brugge’s new goalkeeper Yann Sommer. He’s just had a serious rush of blood to the head and was punished by Nicolas Jackson, who had an easy task to score Villa’s third goal. Sommer has probably ended his team’s hopes of a result here.

Club Brugge 1 Aston Villa 3 (Jackson) A shocker from Brugge, but in particular Sommer. Jackson adds a third for Aston Villa after Sommer comes rushing out of his box! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/HZ1x3BkfK0

A really sloppy piece bit of play from Vanakan who cedes possession to Jackson and he’s straight into Brugge’s backline. He releases the ball to McGinn but the midfielder’s looping cross is cleared. Brugge need to take better care with the detail on their passes.

Jackson escapes the clutches of his marker on the half-way line with a deft spin and he feeds McGinn whose shot is blocked. The ball is worked to Hemmings after Torres is afforded space once more and a block takes it behind for a corner. Villa go short but the routine comes to nothing.

Maatsen flashes a dangerous delivery across the face of goal but the ball bisects Jackson and Buendia precisely and Brugge are able to clear their lines.

Unai Emery is expecting big things from the Brazilian midfielder, who departed relegated Wolves for £38m in July.

Close! Hemmings races on to a cutback but his effort trickles just wide of the post.

Sommer with an accidental handball outside his area! 😳📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/fBbqPEYyUJ

Club Brugge 0 Aston Villa 1 (McGinn) Brugge will be really disappointed with that. Torres is afforded the freedom of Flanders as he strides up from his own half to the edge of the hosts’ box. It is that duo again, Virgili and Seys. They have responded to Wan-Bissaka’s advanced position and are trying to pin him back. Virgili cuts in on to his right foot and forces a save from Suzuki to get the home fans going.

Aston Villa are still establishing their identity with a new team but it has already become clear how much they will rely on goalkeeper Zion Suzuki,

Aston Villa 2.0 is clearly a work in progress after so many high-profile exits and 10 new signings.

Unai Emery has warned that it will take time for his new team to click, but this is an opportunity to spark the season into life.

Behind the scenes, Villa are feeling very comfortable about so much upheaval and it is the presence of Emery in the technical area which provides them with so much optimism.

For a deeper dive into why patience will be needed, read more here.

Brugge have conceded just two goals in five league games this season, but their Pro League opponents have threatened against the Belgian champions’ right side, especially in attacking transitions. Kyriani Sabbe is the more adventurous of Brugge’s two full-backs and the space he vacates will be inviting to George Hemmings and Ian Maatsen.

Here are a couple of examples of Brugge’s vulnerability down their right:

Don-Angelo Konadu, Lommel’s centre-forward, drifts out to the left and takes on Lee Han-beom whose centre-back partner Brandon Mechele has committed too far forward. As such, the space between Lee and covering left-back Joaquin Seys is too big and Freddie Potts attempts to recover from midfield. Konadu earns himself a yard with a feint inside and his shot is well-saved by Yann Sommer.

In Brugge’s 2-1 defeat by Gent a week earlier, Leonardo Lopes punches in a pass into the left half-space for Monodu Sonko to latch on to and from there the inside forward draws a save from Sommer. Josué Vergara’s follow-up strikes the crossbar.

The Spaniard added a fifth Europa League title to his CV last season while also guiding Villa to a strong fourth-place finish in the Premier League. Emery was today announced as one of five nominees for France Football’s Men’s Coach of the Year award – one of the Ballon d’Or accolades.

Christos Tzolis enjoyed an outstanding season with Brugge in 2025-26, contributing 51 goal involvements in 52 matches. His haul earned him a £34m move to Arsenal, where he has continued in much the same vein, laying on three assists in four matches.

While Tzolis wears the No 17 at Arsenal, his former No 8 shirt at Brugge has been inherited by Englishman Freddie Potts, who made the move from West Ham to Belgium last month. Potts has made a strong start to the season, serving as Brugge’s midfield sentry and starting all five of the club’s matches thus far.

One player to keep an eye on for Club Brugge is midfielder Freddie Potts.

He was signed from West Ham last month for a significant fee and lifted the Europa Conference League trophy when David Moyes was in charge.

Also in the Brugge team is Carlos Forbs, the former Manchester City trainee who had a poor loan spell at Wolves a couple of seasons back.

One player who will have many memories of this stadium is Villa centre-back Tyrone Mings.

Who can forget that bewildering moment in November 2024 when Mings picked up the ball inside the penalty area?

Club Brugge are awarded a penalty after Tyrone Mings picks the ball up inside his own area 😳📺 @tntsports & @discoveryplusUK pic.twitter.com/wpAqjMW8pn

Everybody loves a redemption story and on his return a few months later he produced a brilliant individual performance which included an incredible goal-line clearance to save his team.

Mings is on the bench today. Matty Cash is out with a muscle issue so there is a first start for summer signing Aaron Wan-Bissaka.

Addressing the media in Monday’s pre-match press conference, Unai Emery was asked about the challenges of taking Aston Villa into another season in Europe with a significantly changed squad. He said: “To continue in this level, changing some players, key players, but those key players we changed this year as well before the last year we were changing – not like this year, because this year was more players than normal, but we are replacing them.

“We have the players with experience like here with Emiliano [Buendía] and they deserve to continue here trying take now more responsibility and try to give the players we have … Of course we have now new players with a lot of experience like Goretska for example, and we have some young players, they are coming from [big] clubs like Garnacho, Mbaye or Jackson. We must try to adapt them in our structure tactically and arrive [at that point] as fast as possible … We need time, I don’t know if we need time or not, it’s not for me something I’m thinking about, I am thinking about competing. To compete [in] each match.

“We started the Premier League, the first competition, as our objective at the end of the season, because through it we can achieve our objectives this year, and we’re progressing. Still not enough, because we are not getting good results. But [the match against Brugge] is a new test.”

The experienced Yann Sommer starts between the sticks, with in-form striker Nicolò Tresoldi leading the line. English midfielder Freddie Potts is one of Ivan Leko’s two pivots.

How we start this evening to take on Club Brugge in the #UCL 👊 pic.twitter.com/d7ftzgnoIi

Aston Villa are back in the Champions League and in familiar territory with an unfamiliar team.

This will be their third match at the Jan BreydelStadion in less than two years but much has changed with the players that last competed here for Unai Emery.

Two of the goalscorers in the club’s last outing in Bruges were Leon Bailey and Marco Asensio, who are no longer at the club.

Of course, they are not the only players that have left and this is a new-look Emery team hoping for lift-off this season.

Villa are the Europa League winners but this could be a tricky evening against the Belgian Pro League champions.

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of Aston Villa’s Champions League opener against Club Brugge. Unai Emery’s side voyage across the Channel to face the Belgian champions having triumphed in last season’s Europa League and finished fourth in the Premier League. The Villa mothership has since sailed into choppy waters, though, with a raft of big-name sales preceding a run of two defeats and a draw in the league. An opening-weekend thrashing by Brighton and Hove Albion proved quite the storm for Emery’s new-look crew.

Morgan Rogers alighted for Chelsea in a deal worth £117m, a record fee for an English player, and goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez followed soon after, while Youri Tielemans moved to Manchester United. Ezri Konsa and Ollie Watkins completed the exodus of leading men with late-August moves to Arsenal and Al-Hilal respectively. To remedy the outgoings, Villa twice broke their transfer record this summer, pipping Newcastle United to the signing of Johan Manzambi (£59.5m) before landing Nicolas Jackson (£65m, including add-ons), and added Taylor Harwood-Bellis and Ibrahim Mbaye on deadline day. Whether they can hit the ground running remains to be seen, but Emery has a task on his hands aligning his new recruits before the scrutiny intensifies.

Although Villa swept aside Brugge 6-1 across two legs in the Champions League quarter-finals two seasons ago, here Blauw-Zwart (Blue-Black) represent a stern test having made the Jan Breydel Stadium a fortress in last year’s tournament. Their only home defeat in the league phase came against Arsenal, with a 3-3 draw against Barcelona backed up by 4-1 and 3-0 victories over Monaco and Marseille respectively. Belgium’s second-most decorated club have won seven of the last 11 league titles and know how to win matches. In Yann Sommer, Ivan Leko has one of world football’s most experienced goalkeepers, who kept the most clean sheets in the 2024-25 edition of the Champions League (seven). Captain Hans Vanakan, Brandon Mechele and Joaquin Seys were part of Rudi Garcia’s Belgium World Cup squad, and German striker Nicolò Tresoldi already has four goals in six matches this term. English midfielder Freddie Potts could also feature, having settled in nicely in West Flanders having moved from West Ham United during the summer.

The earlier 5.45pm kick-off time, means Villa, Brugge, LASK and AEK Athens have the opportunity to top the 36-team league …at least for a couple of hours.

#1648. GdS: From a curse to a blessing – the factors behind Milan’s recent derby dominance

AC Milan won the derby again on Saturday night, continuing their recent dominance of the fixture, despite Inter celebrating more silverware.

La Gazzetta dello Sport write that Milan planted their flag in the middle of the Duomo and have not removed it for two years. Something strange is happening in the city, frankly inexplicable: Inter haven’t won in eight derbies, even though on paper they’re almost always the stronger team.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Since September 2024, the Nerazzurri have had eight matches against Milan, losing six and drawing too. But why does this keep happening? The paper have attempted to offer some explanations.

Between January 2023 and April 2024, Inter won six consecutive derbies. It became Stefano Pioli’s curse. Three matches were more difficult than the others: the two 2023 Champions League semi-finals and the April 2024 derby, in which Simone Inzaghi’s side sealed the Scudetto.

It was the pinnacle for Inter fans and the worst nightmare for Milan fans, not coincidentally commemorated last night by the Nord with its choreography. From that moment on, Milan turned things around.

In September 2024, they won with Matteo Gabbia’s 89th-minute header, and it all changed from there. A pair of draws, then the 3-0 Coppa Italia win with a Luka Jovic brace, the two 1-0 wins last season (Pulisic in the first leg, Estupinan in the return), and this 3-1 win most recently.

For the reasons, you should consult a psychologist, but some things can be understood. Milan certainly play much more freely than during those terrible 15 months.

They’re definitely finding tactical solutions they didn’t have in that run under Pioli, where they pressed hard and ended up only allowing counter-attacks. They especially struggled greatly against Dimarco, Calhanoglu, and Mkhitaryan.

Paulo Fonseca initiated the change, reinforced by Sergio Conceiçao in the Supercoppa Italiana final, by Massimiliano Allegri, and now by Amorim. Milan are increasingly confident and, as much as possible in a crazy situation like the derby, control the games.

This time, they struggled very little, even in the second half, as if they had the password to counter Inter’s moves. Much of it was a question of energy: Milan no longer fear their cousins, they go head-to-head, and often win the duels in recent derbies.

Then, of course, there are the individuals. Christian Pulisic is becoming a ghost for Inter, fitting of these times. CP11 has scored in four of the last eight derbies, and they’ve all been crucial goals. With his intelligence, he understands where to strike Inter. With his speed, he surprises them.

As for that intelligence thing, Luka Modric is second to none. In the derby that Pervis Estupinan won, he was the best on the field. In Saturday’s resounding win, he helped the team manage the tempo, defended up front, winning back valuable balls, and even left the free kick to Moreira.

Add Adrien Rabiot to the list of Inter nightmares: ‘the Duke’ has earned 7.5, 7, and 7.5 again in the three Milan derbies he has played (Gazzetta ratings). Throwing all that together, and you get a one-sided fixture.

#1643. Jordan Henderson smirks as he trolls Anfield boo-boys on return with Chelsea - and argues with ex-Liverpool team-mate Virgil van Dijk

Published: 19:47 EDT, 28 October 2026 | Updated: 20:51 EDT, 28 October 2026

Jordan Henderson laughed off his haters on his return to Anfield on Wednesday night.

Liverpool legend Henderson, 36, played the full 90 minutes of the Carabao Cup last-16 tie as Chelsea lost 6-5 on penalties, although the veteran did score his spot kick.

It capped what must have been a strange night for the midfielder as he went back to the club where he made 492 appearances and won eight trophies over a 12-year period. Henderson left to join Saudi Arabian side Al-Ettifaq in the summer of 2023.

Despite his long service, Henderson received a vociferous reception as a Chelsea player, with the home faithful booing him every time he touched the ball.

And, after the Blues were awarded a penalty in the first half when Ryan Gravenberch fouled Moises Caicedo, that atmosphere escalated further.

Henderson picked up the ball and walked towards the penalty spot as if he was going to take the spot kick.

Hendo smirking at Liverpool fans in a Chelsea shirt. Never thought we'd see the daypic.twitter.com/Fac2gSbe5x

Jordan Henderson was seen smirking after receiving a hostile reception from Liverpool fans

The former Liverpool captain also argued with his former team-mate Virgil van Dijk at one point

As he did so, Henderson was loudly jeered and he allowed himself a wry smile and laugh as he looked back towards the crowd.

Henderson ultimately handed the ball over to Morgan Rogers, who made no mistake from the spot.

The hostile reception may have been in part motivated by the midfielder's desire to contest several decisions with Liverpool's players and referee Darren England, along with the fact he is now representing Chelsea.

At one point early in the first half, both Henderson and his former team-mate Virgil van Dijk fought their case in one discussion with England.

As they walked away, the pair shouted at each other from afar in what must have been a strange sight for Liverpool supporters to witness.

Henderson did later appear to applaud the crowd after the game when he was also seen laughing and joking with van Dijk.

Meanwhile, at the end of last season, Henderson, who has similarly played for Ajax and Brentford in recent years, returned to Anfield for the first time with the Bees.

On that occasion, he received a warm reception and then a standing ovation when he was substituted in the second half.

Speaking after that game, he wrote on social media: 'I'd like to thank the Liverpool fans for the reception they gave me yesterday.

'It meant a lot to me going back to Anfield and being able to say thank you for everything you gave me in my 12 years at the club. It's a feeling that I'll never forget.

'To be able to be there to see my two brothers, Mo [Salah] and Robbo [Andy Robertson], say goodbye and get the send-off they deserve was also special.

'We spent some amazing times together that I will cherish forever. I wish you both all the very best in your next chapters.'

#1639. Ezri Konsa, the best Arsenal signing of last window, gives Mikel Arteta a welcome selection headache

By Alexis Pereira | 02 Nov 2026 19:29

Arsenal’s outstanding defensive display in the 1-0 win over Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday ended a 14-year wait for a Premier League victory at their rival’s ground. The result was built on superb organisation and discipline in front of David Raya’s goal, and one of the standout names was Ezri Konsa.

The England defender produced a top-level performance to secure the clean sheet. According to Opta, he won eight of nine duels, made eight clearances, five tackles, five recoveries and two blocks, and won two fouls.

For the first time in the Premier League era, Liverpool did not register a single shot on target in a game at Anfield, a mark that highlights the outstanding collective defending and the performance of the centre-back pairing. Konsa’s understanding with Gabriel Magalhaes makes it look as though the two have played together for many seasons.

So far, Konsa has maintained the high level he showed at his former club, Aston Villa. He has made only 13 appearances for the Gunners this season, yet he already merits the label of a successful signing. His assured displays have almost made supporters forget who held the position before his arrival.

The 29-year-old joined Arsenal in August for £51m to replace William Saliba, who suffered a serious back injury that forced him off in the World Cup semi-final between France and Spain.

Saliba, who is not expected to return until the end of this month, had been one of Arsenal’s defensive foundations in recent seasons, and the club decided to bring in an outside name, even though Christian Mosquera, Piero Hincapie, Riccardo Calafiori and Jurrien Timber could all have played there.

From here, boss Mikel Arteta will have the kind of selection headache every manager dreams of. Konsa and Saliba will compete at a high level to play alongside Gabriel Magalhaes, and Arsenal can only benefit.

The season is long and the Gunners will compete for every trophy. Having elite players both on the pitch and on the bench is essential to withstand the physical strain over the months ahead.

In recent seasons, Arsenal have made good signings, especially in defence, such as Timber, Calafiori and Hincapie. Konsa shares a key characteristic with those names. His versatility, as he can also play at right-back, gives Arteta a range of options very few European clubs can match, and over a long season that could prove decisive.

#1632. 'Bournemouth is incredible - in summer it feels like I'm back in Brazil!': EVANILSON on taking down Man United and AC Milan, Marco Rose's 'high expectations', leaving home at 13 and drawing his late mother every day

Published: 22:00 EDT, 28 October 2026 | Updated: 22:00 EDT, 28 October 2026

A storm was swirling around Old Trafford, Senne Lammens had been left behind and the angle had all but closed.

Evanilson has been drawing perfect lines since he was a child in Fortaleza in Brazil’s Northeast region, pausing cartoons on the television to copy them on to paper. Last Sunday he drew one more – arcing violently into the Manchester United net.

'When I thought about going past the goalkeeper, I just took a chance,' he tells Daily Mail Sport. 'It was very windy, too. Maybe the wind helped, but I went for the perfect angle there. I managed to score that goal, which was very difficult, but it was beautiful.'

The goal in question capped a 3-0 win, Bournemouth's fourth in a row without conceding and the third time in four seasons they’d won at Old Trafford by that scoreline. Three days earlier, Evanilson's flicked header led to the penalty that kickstarted a 3-0 win over AC Milan in the Europa League.

In 2008, Bournemouth began a season in the fourth tier with a 17-point deduction. Now they are in Europe for the first time, at a stadium that holds about 12,400, in red and black stripes borrowed from Milan more than 50 years ago.

'For our club, for all the players, beating two world giants is always very special,' says Evanilson, 27. 'A very important week for us. I think we're quite confident for the rest of the season. It helped us a lot.'

Evanilson goes around Manchester United goalkeeper Senne Lammens...

...arcs an audacious effort into the top corner to make it 3-0 to Bournemouth...

...and celebrates another milestone win for the club in what was surely the greatest week in its history

The strike at Old Trafford was Evanilson's fourth in five games, a week after his 100th career goal against Sunderland. Asked to give it a mark out of five, he goes further.

'For me, this is one of the most beautiful,' he says. 'Even more so because of the size of the game, against United, away from home, at Old Trafford. That pushes the score even higher.'

The week could get better still. Carlo Ancelotti names his Brazil squad on Thursday, and Evanilson, whose two caps for his country came in 2024, has never been called up by the Italian. With Chelsea No9 Joao Pedro injured, Brentford’s Igor Thiago out of form and Richarlison out of favour at Tottenham, will this be Evanilson’s time?

'Of course, I'm always thinking about the national team,’ he says. ‘I think it's the hunger of every player, to always be wearing the biggest shirt of all national teams. My expectation is high. I hope to be able to be there. If not, keep working, keep doing my part. Who knows, one day.'

Not long ago, a week like this looked a distant prospect. Andoni Iraola left in the summer after taking Bournemouth to sixth place and a first European qualification. His successor, Marco Rose, took seven league games to get his first win, after a 5-1 defeat at Chelsea on October 10 left his side 17th.

Under Rose, Evanilson presses from the front and has at times dropped behind another striker. He has four goals and four assists in 11 games in the Premier League and Europa League.

'For me, there's no such thing as a lost ball,' he says. 'I'm always running, making movements up front. I work for the team. The manager has fitted us well into this team, and now we know what he really wants from us. He wants mobility up front, he wants us to press high. It's no coincidence that we won these last four games, and won well, without conceding.'

Iraola, now at Liverpool, taught Evanilson about life in the Premier League after he joined for a club-record £40million from Porto two years ago.

Andoni Iraola, now at Liverpool, taught Evanilson about life in the Premier League after he joined for a club-record £40million from Porto two years ago

Marco Rose, Iraola's successor, has set Evanilson a target of 15 to 20 goals this season

Evanilson reacts to Justin Kluivert opening the scoring against AC Milan last week, kickstarting a historic 3-0 win for the Cherries

'He helped me a lot to adapt to English football, which is totally different,' says Evanilson. 'With this intensity, he helped me a lot with pressing, with making movements to try to break down my opponent. He's Spanish, and I don't speak fluent English, but he spoke to me in Spanish. I'm very grateful to him.'

'At the start it's always difficult, even for him, to adapt to English football,' Evanilson says. 'In some games he tells us to do certain things and we don't do them, and we suffer for it. He knows what he's doing, he plans the games very well, and the intensity on the pitch is also very similar to Iraola's. He trusts me a lot.'

The German has said Evanilson can score 15 to 20 goals this season, after 18 in his first two campaigns combined.

'The expectation he has is very high,' says Evanilson. 'I'm sure more chances will keep coming. I have to be there, I have to be focused to convert them.'

Evanilson’s compatriot Rayan also scored at Old Trafford, his first league goal of the season. The 20-year-old joined from Vasco da Gama in January in a deal worth an initial £24.7m and started for Brazil at the World Cup.

'I already knew the quality he had as a player, but I didn't know him as a person,' says Evanilson. 'He's an impeccable lad, a good guy. We're always together here at the club. He's a player with a lot of strength, explosiveness, and he also has that nose for goal. Since he arrived, I've tried to help him so he could adapt faster.'

At Porto, Evanilson was the one being helped. Having joined for around £8m in 2020 from Fluminense, he spent much of his first year in Portugal with the B team. Pepe, the former Real Madrid centre back, kept him going.

Legendary former Real Madrid centre back Pepe (centre) was the guiding light for Evanilson (left) when his Porto career took a while to get going

But eventually the striker found his place and scored 60 goals in 154 Porto appearances, earning him his move to the Premier League

'Love him, love him,' he says of Pepe. 'He was always talking to me. He'd say: "Calm down, your time will come, the coach really likes you." Sometimes I'd get sad. I'd been signed and I was playing for Porto B.'

Porto won the league and cup double the following season, and Evanilson scored 21 goals in all competitions. Two years later he was on his way to England.

Bournemouth is a very long way from home, but he had learned about distance long before, leaving Fortaleza for Fluminense in Rio de Janeiro – 1,600 miles and a day and a half’s drive away at the opposite tip of Brazil.

'It's very hard for us to leave the Northeast,' he says. 'When I left there at 13, I was a kid, I left on my own. Sometimes I wanted to go back.

'And my mother told me all the time: "If you want to be a footballer, you have to face reality, you have to keep going. You're a good player, but this part off the pitch, you have to overcome it."'

Jose Neto, the coach who took him to Rio, has said the boy promised to draw his mother, Madalena, every day to ease the homesickness. She died suddenly in 2017 when Evanilson was in the Fluminense youth academy, and he thought about giving up football.

'I'd like her to be living all of this that I've been through, from when I left Fortaleza to where I am now,' he says. 'I'm sure she's proud. The only thing I'd really like is for her to be able to be here, living it and watching me play in the Premier League.'

The drawing never stopped. These days he does it with his daughter, Maria Alice.

Bournemouth team-mate and compatriot Rayan has nailed down a place in the Brazil starting XI - now Evanilson wants to follow suit

Evanilson moved more than 1,600 miles from his home city of Fortaleza to join the Fluminense academy in Rio de Janeiro

'Whenever I'm at home with her, we try to do some drawing,' he says. 'It makes me relax, it makes me forget some problems. And it's really nice to know that she likes it too.'

Home in Bournemouth also means Ola Brasil, a small shop on Wimborne Road whose owner delivered rice, beans, chicken and farofa, a toasted cassava flour, to the family's hotel when they arrived.

'That food every Brazilian loves, when you go a while without eating it, you even feel weak,' he says.

It is the only place he can find Brazilian-style Maria biscuits.

'I always buy them,' he says. 'My one-year-old son only eats these Maria biscuits. He's crazy about them.'

He has always lived by the sea, in Fortaleza, Rio, Porto and now Dorset, where the water is a bit different.

‘It’s impossible to go in because of the cold water. Very, very cold,’ he says.

The sea he grew up with is in Brazil’s Northeast, a region of nine states along the Atlantic. Fortaleza, with about 2.6million people, is its biggest city. Evanilson still goes back with his family.

Evanilson has two Brazil caps to his name, and is hoping to win his first call-up under Carlo Ancelotti this week

‘In summer (Bournemouth) is incredible, it gets up to 35 degrees, and it’s nice. Sometimes, in summer, you can feel like you’re in Brazil, in our Northeast’

‘Our Northeast is incredible, very beautiful,’ he says. ‘Even though it’s very hot, it’s very beautiful, it’s perfect, it has beautiful beaches. I loved living there. Whenever I go to Fortaleza, I always want to be on the beach. Even the water temperature helps you relax.

‘The town here is very good too. In summer, it’s a really hot town. Lots of people from other cities in England come to spend the summer here. The beaches are always full, the streets packed, and the heat here is similar too.’

On the hottest days, the distance to his homeland shrinks.

‘In summer it’s incredible, it gets up to 35°C, and it’s nice. Sometimes, in summer, you can feel like you’re in Brazil, in our Northeast.’

#1630. Barcelona's Gavi stance 'revealed' amid transfer speculation surrounding 22-year-old

By Matt Law | 02 Nov 2026 19:49

Barcelona are reportedly unwilling to discuss an exit for Gavi, with the club viewing the midfielder as a vital player despite his struggles for action this term.

The 22-year-old has been restricted to just 191 minutes of football across seven appearances for Barcelona at the start of the 2026-27 campaign.

The Spaniard has only started twice in La Liga this term, while his three appearances in the Champions League have come off the bench.

There is currently a host of speculation surrounding Gavi's future, with some reports claiming that the midfielder could be allowed to leave Camp Nou for the right price.

However, according to transfer expert Fabrizio Romano, Barcelona have no desire to allow Gavi to leave, viewing the Spaniard as an important part of their plans moving forward.

Barcelona head coach Hansi Flick was asked about Gavi during his press conference on Monday, with the team preparing to face Aston Villa in the Champions League on Tuesday.

“We all know his quality and Gavi is always an option, but once the match starts that option might disappear and you can’t always stick to your initial plan. I’ve spoken to him and the important thing is that he has confidence," Flick told reporters.

Gavi has been with Barcelona since the age of 11, progressing to the first team in 2021, and he has represented the Catalan outfit on 173 occasions, scoring 10 goals and registering 18 assists for the club in all competitions.

Worryingly, Gavi has already had two severe knee injuries in the early stages of his career, first being absent between November 2023 and September 2024.

Gavi was also missing between August 2025 and March 2026, and fitness problems have made it difficult for him to find consistency in recent seasons.

It is understood that a number of major clubs are keeping a close eye on the situation in the event that Barcelona signal a willingness to let him depart.

Barcelona will follow Tuesday's clash against Villa with a La Liga fixture away to Atletico Madrid ahead of the November international break.
